    // FIXME: query don't use domain repo, because it is used for triggering business logic
    type GetNote struct {
        ID             uuid.UUID
        ExcludeTrashed bool
    
        UserID string
    }
    
    type GetNoteHandler struct {
        authorizationSvc AuthorizationSvc
        noteRepo         domain.NoteRepo
        readModel        GetNoteReadModel
    }
    
    func NewGetNoteHandler(
        authorizationSvc AuthorizationSvc,
        noteRepo domain.NoteRepo,
        readModel GetNoteReadModel,
    ) *GetNoteHandler {
        return &GetNoteHandler{
            authorizationSvc: authorizationSvc,
            noteRepo:         noteRepo,
            readModel:        readModel,
        }
    }
    
    var ProvideGetNoteHandler = NewGetNoteHandler
    
    type GetNoteQuery commonhandler.Query[GetNote, *Note]
    
    var _ GetNoteQuery = (*GetNoteHandler)(nil)
    
    func (h *GetNoteHandler) Handle(ctx context.Context, query *GetNote) (*Note, error) {
        workspaceID, err := h.noteRepo.GetWorkspaceIDByID(ctx, query.ID)
        if err != nil {
            return nil, err
        }
        hasPermission, err := h.authorizationSvc.HasWorkspaceItemPermission(
            ctx,
            query.UserID,
            workspaceID,
            WorkspaceItemPermissionRead,
        )
        if err != nil {
            return nil, err
        }
        if !hasPermission {
            return nil, errs.NewForbidden(
                fmt.Sprintf("user %s does not have permission to read note %s", query.UserID, query.ID),
            )
        }
        note, err := h.readModel.Handle(ctx, &GetNoteReadModelParams{
            ID:             query.ID,
            ExcludeTrashed: query.ExcludeTrashed,
        })
        return note, err
    }

## Assistant

I’ve explored the scoped `AGENTS.md` files, [previous session notes](/home/ntgnguyen/Projects/notopia/ai_chat_session.md), AI backend, assistant UI, editor integration, and service contracts. No code changed.

The main findings:

- **Search needs fixing first.** [SearchService](/home/ntgnguyen/Projects/notopia/apps/ai/src/search/search.service.ts) does not scope searches to the authenticated user. Omitting `workspaceId` queries the index without a workspace filter.
- **The assistant cannot read attached note content yet.** Attachments send names and IDs; `getNote` returns metadata only. Content belongs to the document service.
- **No throttle is currently implemented** in the AI service.
- **`toolChoice: 'none'` is already absent.** Keep automatic tool selection.
- **Tool availability is currently static:** every request receives all three custom tools plus any supplied BlockNote definitions.
- **A commit button already exists**, but it is an icon shown only when modified. Committing also updates searchable content and graph links.
- Some AI guidance is stale: it describes the removed web proxy and a different step limit.

My proposed implementation order:

1. **Secure and validate AI requests**
   - Validate messages, tool definitions, IDs, and request size at runtime—the current DTO supplies TypeScript types only.
   - Enforce workspace access before searching; build filters from validated, authorized workspace IDs.
   - Exclude trashed results and bound returned content.
   - Reserve server tool names so client definitions cannot alter their meaning.

2. **Add shared throttling and consistent errors**
   - Use Redis for limits shared across AI instances, keyed primarily by authenticated user ID.
   - Add IP limits only after checking the trusted proxy chain. Client IP should come from gateway forwarding, rather than assuming Authentik supplies it.
   - Include concurrent-stream limits, cancellation, and configurable generation limits.
   - Before streaming, return meaningful HTTP statuses and a consistent application error body. During streaming, use AI SDK error parts.

   AI SDK defines a streaming error protocol, but arbitrary HTTP JSON errors are not automatically converted into your application error type. The installed transport reads failed HTTP responses as text. We should normalize those responses in a shared transport. Tool execution failures should appear as tool failures; BlockNote also has an AI error/retry state. See [AI SDK error handling](https://ai-sdk.dev/docs/ai-sdk-ui/error-handling) and [tool errors](https://ai-sdk.dev/docs/ai-sdk-core/tools-and-tool-calling).

3. **Introduce a tool registry and useful read tools**

   | Tool | Purpose | Work needed |
   |---|---|---|
   | `listWorkspaces` | Discover accessible workspaces | Improve existing tool |
   | `searchNotes` | Find relevant notes with excerpts | Fix authorization and filtering |
   | `getNoteMetadata` | Read title, tags, and location | Clarify existing `getNote` |
   | `readNoteContent` | Read actual note content | Add document-service internal contract |
   | `getWorkspaceTree` | Browse folders and notes | Expose existing use case through gRPC |
   | `getNoteLinks` | Explore backlinks and related notes | Expose existing use case through gRPC |

   Select tools per request context and permissions, then recheck permission during execution. Internal calls should follow the repository’s gRPC rule.

4. **Connect the assistant to editor tools**
   - Add shared context for service URLs.
   - Build a sidebar assistant connected to the active editor.
   - Reuse BlockNote’s exported editing integration through an adapter. Its documented `chatProvider` supports sharing a chat instance; the integration still needs verification against installed BlockNote `0.55.0`. See [BlockNote AI reference](https://github.com/typecellos/blocknote/blob/main/docs/content/docs/features/ai/reference.mdx).
   - For other notes, lazily create editor sessions connected to their Yjs documents, with permission checks and cleanup. Mounting every file’s editor upfront would be expensive.
   - Make **Commit changes** explicit and accessible, with pending/error feedback.

5. **Keep subscription ownership separate**
   - My recommendation is for billing to own plans, subscriptions, and entitlements; authorization continues owning workspace permissions.
   - AI consumes entitlements and meters usage. Redis throttling handles bursts; durable usage accounting handles subscription quotas.
   - Defer building billing until plan rules are defined.

I recommend implementing **steps 1–3 first**, followed by the sidebar and editing integration. Validation should cover cross-workspace access, malformed requests, shared throttling, stream/tool failures, and editor changes through commit, alongside affected lint and typechecks.

    # Billing Service
    
    Plans, prices, subscriptions, entitlements. Stripe (sandbox) through hosted Checkout and
    Customer Portal. DDD + CQRS like `internal/note`, but without an outbox.
    Entrypoint: `cmd/billing/`. HTTP spec: `api/billing/`. gRPC: `proto/billing/`.
    Spec and plans: `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-10-11-billing-03-*`, `docs/superpowers/plans/2026-10-11-billing-03-*`.
    
    ## Layers
    
    | Dir | Contains | Rules |
    | --- | --- | --- |
    | `domain/` | Aggregates (`Subscription` + `Refund`, `BillingAccount`, `Price`, `Plan`, `BillingPolicy`), `ResolveEntitlements`, repo interfaces, `UnitOfWork`, `ProviderEventLog` | Pure. `uint8` enums with `IsValid`/`String` |
    | `app/` | `cmd_*` / `q_*` use cases, ports (`svc_*`, `readmodel.go`), app models | Commands use `domain.UnitOfWork`; queries use `app.BillingReadModel` only |
    | `infra/` | `persistence/` (pgrepo, pgreadmodel, pgmapper, pgjsonb, pgsqlc, pgmigration), `notifier/` (Kafka), `service/` (authorization gRPC), `redis/` | Each adapter maps enums explicitly (`toX`/`fromX`), never casts |
    | `controller/` | `http/` (gin strict server, Stripe webhook), `grpc/`, `event/` (Kafka consumers, one consumer group per topic, typed via `decode[T]`), `cron/`, `health/` | Thin — translate, don't decide |
    | `component/` | Validator, `eventtopic.go` (every topic published or consumed) | No inline topic strings elsewhere |
    | `errs/` | Typed errors (`Code` is the wire code) | Mapped in `controller/http/err.go` and `controller/grpc/err.go` |
    
    ## Persistence
    
    - Write side: `pgsqlc/<aggregate>.sql`, lock-aware via `FOR UPDATE -- :if @for_update` (dynamic filter plugin).
    - Read side: `pgsqlc/<aggregate>_read.sql`, every query named `Read…`, used only by `pgreadmodel`.
    - `plans.features` / `plans.limits` are typed JSONB (`pgjsonb.Features`/`Limits`); unknown keys are skipped with a warning.
    - Webhook de-duplication (`processed_provider_events`) is part of `RepoRegistry`, so "processed" commits with its effect.
    
    ## Stripe
    
    - Sandbox only. Stripe does not onboard VN businesses for live payouts; a VN gateway can replace it behind `app.PaymentProvider`.
    - Webhooks are fetch-and-sync: payloads are used for ids only, state is read back from Stripe, so ordering does not matter.
    - Every Stripe write that must not duplicate carries an idempotency key (`customer:{workspaceId}`, `refund:{refundId}`, `price:{priceId}`).
    - Webhook use-case ordering: provider reads and idempotent mutations that must not be lost (change default card) run **before** the write transaction; cancelling a subscription runs **after** the local cancel commits (failures are logged, and reconcile retries canceled rows the provider has not confirmed); the transaction records the event (`ProviderEventLog.MarkProcessed`) with the state change; refunds run **after** commit via `RefundRunner` and the reconcile cron retries `pending` refunds without a provider id.
    - `PaymentProvider` is the only port to Stripe; stripe-go is imported only in `infra/payment/stripe` and `controller/http/webhook.go`.
    
    ## Local development
    
    - Keys: `cmd/billing/.env.local` (`NOTOPIA_BILLING_STRIPE_SECRET_KEY`, `NOTOPIA_BILLING_STRIPE_WEBHOOK_SECRET`), `cmd/billingseed/.env.local` (`NOTOPIA_BILLINGSEED_STRIPE_SECRET_KEY`).
    - `just seed-billing`: Stripe products/prices + portal configuration, idempotent (needed in every environment).
    - `just fixtures-billing`: dev-only workspace with fake Stripe ids (no Stripe calls).
    - `just stripe-listen`: forwards sandbox events to `http://api.notopia.localhost/billing/webhooks/stripe`; put the printed `whsec_` in `.env.local`.
    - Test cards: `4242 4242 4242 4242` (succeeds), `4000 0000 0000 0341` (card saves, charge fails → `past_due`), `4000 0025 0000 3155` (3-D Secure), `4000 0000 0000 9995` (declined). Any future expiry and CVC.
    - Full manual walkthrough: `tmp/TEST_FLOW_BILLING.md`; diagrams: `docs/src/references/sequence/billing.md`.
    
    ## Notifications
    
    `events.integration.billing.subscription.changed` is **best-effort**: published straight to Kafka after
    `uow.Execute` returns, errors only logged. Consumers never cache billing state; they call gRPC on every check.
    
    ## Crons
    
    `controller/cron/`, Redis-locked on `billing_redis`: hourly reconcile, daily prune of processed provider events.
    Each job is configured by `NOTOPIA_BILLING_CRON_{RECONCILE_SUBSCRIPTIONS|PRUNE_PROVIDER_EVENTS}_{NAME|SCHEDULE|TIMEOUT|ENABLED}` (defaults in `config.New`; `..._ENABLED=false` disables).
    `// NOTE:` move into `cmd/billing-worker` when splitting.

    # AI Service (nx: `ai`)
    
    Stateless BlockNote AI backend. NestJS HTTP in (no Kafka, no DB); it is a
    gRPC *client* of the note service and an HTTP client of Meilisearch for custom
    tools. Receives `{ messages, toolDefinitions }` from the web proxy, streams
    back an AI SDK v6 UI-message stream via an OpenAI-compatible LLM.
    
    ## Modules (`src/`)
    
    | Module | Note |
    | --- | --- |
    | `ai/` | `AiController` (`POST /ai`), `AiService` (streamText + BlockNote + custom tools), `tools/` (see `HOW_TO_ADD_TOOLS.md`) |
    | `note/` | gRPC client for the note service (same pattern as `apps/document/src/note/`) |
    | `authorization/` | gRPC client for the authorization service |
    | `search/` | `SearchService` — Meilisearch HTTP client (`notes` index) |
    | `common/` | `HttpUserGuard` + `@ReqUser()` — reads Traefik-forwarded `x-forwarded-*` headers |
    | `config.ts`, `config.factory.ts`, `env.validation.ts` | Zod config (`NOTOPIA_AI_*`) |
    
    ## Request flow
    
    Browser (`DefaultChatTransport`, Bearer from better-auth) → `apps/web` `POST /api/ai`
    (proxy, forwards `Authorization`) → Traefik `jwt` middleware (validates, injects
    `x-forwarded-*`) → `POST /ai` (guarded) → OpenAI-compatible LLM → SSE stream back.
    
    `GET /ai/health` is unauthenticated (Traefik bypass, like other services).
    
    ## Things worth knowing
    
    - `toolDefinitionsToToolSet(body.toolDefinitions ?? {})` — the client may omit
      tool definitions; the helper throws on `undefined`.
    - `AiService` returns `result.toUIMessageStream()`; the controller pipes it with
      the official `pipeUIMessageStreamToResponse()` helper ([Nest cookbook](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/vercel/ai/refs/heads/main/content/cookbook/15-api-servers/50-nest.mdx)).
      `await` only resolves headers — chunks stream through as they arrive.
    - LLM is configured via `NOTOPIA_AI_LLM_{BASE_URL,API_KEY,MODEL}` — any
      OpenAI-compatible endpoint (Ollama, vLLM, OpenAI itself).
    - `@ai-sdk/openai-compatible` stays on **v2**: v3 targets the v4 model spec
      (needs `ai` v7) but `@blocknote/xl-ai` pins `ai` v6.
    - Config tokens are Symbols: `ConfigService.get()` needs the raw Symbol
      (`get(SERVICES_CONFIG)`), `@Inject()` needs the factory KEY
      (`@Inject(servicesConfig.KEY)`). Mixing them up fails silently (`undefined`).
    - No OpenAPI spec — the SSE stream doesn't fit `openapi-generator`.
    # Document Service (nx: `document`)
    
    Owns document *content* (note metadata lives in `internal/note`). NestJS: HTTP REST +
    Yjs WebSocket + Kafka producer/consumer. Spec: `api/document/`.
    
    ## Modules (`src/`)
    
    | Module | Note |
    | --- | --- |
    | `document/` | `DocumentEntity` (Yjs state as `bytea` + `modified` flag), commit workflow, attachment URLs |
    | `revision/` | Revision snapshots, paginated read, rename, hard delete |
    | `hocuspocus/` | Yjs server, connection auth, live permission revocation |
    | `blocknote/` | Schema provider + YDoc↔blocks conversion, tag/link extraction |
    | `note/`, `authorization/` | gRPC clients (generated from `proto/`) |
    | `authentication/` | Multi-issuer JWKS validation — for the **WebSocket** token |
    | `common/` | `UserGuard` + `@User()` — for **HTTP**, reads gateway-forwarded headers |
    | `storage/`, `kafka/`, `database/`, `config/` | S3 presign, Kafka client, TypeORM, Zod config |
    
    Two auth paths, easy to trip on: HTTP trusts Traefik's forwarded headers; the WebSocket
    gets a raw JWT in the connect payload and validates it itself in
    `Hocuspocus.onAuthenticate`.
    
    ## The commit pipeline
    
    `DocumentService.commitIfDue()` is the hinge of the whole system. In one transaction
    (pessimistic write lock on the document) it: saves a `RevisionEntity` of the current
    blocks, clears `modified`, and emits
    `events.integration.document.document.committed`. Three callers, one revision when they race
    (row lock + min-interval/hash check):
    
    | Trigger | Caller | Gate |
    | --- | --- | --- |
    | `manual` | `POST /document/documents/{id}/commit` | write permission (viewers 403); always commits changed content |
    | `auto` | `AutoCommitExtension.afterStoreDocument` | plan feature `auto_commit` + `auto_commit_min_interval_seconds` |
    | `sweeper` | `SweeperCron` | stale `modified` docs idle ≥ `idleSeconds`; walks all of them in batches of 500 per tick |
    
    Manual responses: `201 {revisionId}` revision created, `200 {revisionId}` content equals the
    latest revision (returns it), `204` nothing changed and no revision exists. When the content
    hash equals the latest revision only `modified` is cleared; `pendingContributorIds` is kept
    for the next real commit.
    
    Callers clear the in-memory `modified` flag only when the loaded Y.Doc's content hash equals
    the committed one (state vectors miss delete-only edits).
    
    Billing unreachable: auto-commit is skipped (warn), the sweeper and purge skip the batch,
    editing continues.
    
    Downstream: `internal/note` (`e_documentcommitted.go`) updates note size/tags/outgoing
    links; `search-worker` indexes the content into Meilisearch. **Nothing else re-indexes** —
    if a document is never committed, its content is never searchable and its links never
    appear in the graph.
    
    ## Yjs / Hocuspocus
    
    Extension hooks run by descending priority, not array order:
    
    | Extension | Priority | Role |
    | --- | --- | --- |
    | `ContributorFlushExtension` | 1100 | Flushes tracked editors to `pendingContributorIds` in `onStoreDocument`, and retries in `afterStoreDocument` (a brand-new document has no row yet during its first store) |
    | `@hocuspocus/extension-redis` | 1000 | Store lock; an instance missing it throws `SkipFurtherHooksError`, skipping later hooks, hence the flush runs before it |
    | Database (`HocuspocusDatabase`) | 100 | Upserts the row |
    | `AutoCommitExtension` | 50 | Must run after the row is stored. No forced commit on disconnect (the sweeper covers idle docs). Resolves the workspace with `NoteService.batchGetNoteWorkspaces` (no auth, marked `HACK:`; should become a service-account role) |
    
    - `HocuspocusDatabase.store` upserts the row and writes `modified` from the Yjs metadata
      (`DocumentService.upsertData`). Stores are debounced server-wide by
      `NOTOPIA_DOCUMENT_HOCUSPOCUS_DEBOUNCE_MS` (default 2000) and
      `NOTOPIA_DOCUMENT_HOCUSPOCUS_MAX_DEBOUNCE_MS` (default 10000). The manual commit calls
      `HocuspocusService.flushStore` first, so edits still in the debounce are stored before
      `commitIfDue` reads the row.
    - `AutoCommitExtension` skips the note/billing calls when `lastCommittedAt` is less than
      `NOTOPIA_DOCUMENT_AUTO_COMMIT_CHECK_FLOOR_SECONDS` (default 60, the shortest plan interval;
      `0` disables) ago. Only a cheap local precondition, not a cache: the real interval comes
      from the plan's `auto_commit_min_interval_seconds`.
    - `afterLoadDocument` applies the DB `modified` column into the `metadata` Y.Map
      (`YDocMetadataMap`) with origin `{ source: 'local', skipStoreHooks: true }`, so loading
      does not trigger a store. Clients read `{ modified }` from it.
      After a commit, callers use `HocuspocusService.clearModifiedIfCommitted` (or
      `DocumentService.clearModifiedIfCommitted` with the loaded `Y.Doc`), which clears the flag
      only when the loaded doc's content hash equals the committed one, so edits not stored yet
      keep `modified`.
    - `note.deleted` → `HocuspocusService.onNoteDeleted` marks the id in `deletedDocumentIds`
      (the store guard), closes its connections, waits for in-flight stores
      (`waitForPendingStores`) and deletes the row; revisions cascade by FK. Without the guard,
      the final store on unload would upsert the row back. The set only holds loaded documents
      and is cleared in `afterUnloadDocument`, so it does not grow.
      Scaling out: the instance consuming `note.deleted` may not hold the live document, so a
      shared set (Redis) does not help. The event must reach every instance (one consumer group
      per instance, or Hocuspocus Redis extension).
    - `onRoleChanged` / `onMemberRemoved` consume Kafka events from `authorization` and walk
      live connections to flip `readOnly` or close with codes 4001/4002.
    
    ## Crons and locks
    
    `@notopia-uit/lib-server/locks` provides `LocksSetupModule.forRoot({ redisUrl?, ttl? })`.
    With no `redisUrl` it uses an in-memory store (single instance only, a warning is logged, intended even in production, see `packages/lib-server/AGENTS.md`); with one it uses `RedisLockStore`. The lock
    Redis must run with `noeviction` and persistence, and the app must call
    `app.enableShutdownHooks()`. `redis.url` (`NOTOPIA_DOCUMENT_REDIS_URL`) picks the lock store;
    `scaling.enabled` (`NOTOPIA_DOCUMENT_SCALING_ENABLED`, requires the URL) only adds
    `@hocuspocus/extension-redis`. Its clients come from the app's ioredis via `createClient` (the
    extension's own ioredis 5.6.1 parses URLs with the deprecated `url.parse()`). Local compose
    Redis for this service is `document_redis`.
    
    Crons (`src/cron/`) are not `@Cron` decorators (those cannot read config): `CronRegistrar`
    adds them to `SchedulerRegistry` in `onModuleInit` from `NOTOPIA_DOCUMENT_CRON_*` (name = lock
    key, schedule, enabled, timeout seconds), with no `timeZone`, so they run in the process TZ.
    Each tick runs in `Locks.withLock(name, …)`; `LockNotAcquiredError` means another instance has
    it. Jobs get an `AbortSignal` (lock lost or timeout) and stop between batches when it aborts.
    Defaults: `document:sweeper` `*/10 * * * *` (timeout 300 s, idle 600 s),
    `document:revision-purge` `30 3 * * *` (timeout 1800 s); each has `_ENABLED=false` to disable.
    Revision purge deletes revisions older than the plan's `revision_history_days` and always keeps
    the latest one.
    
    ## Revisions are hard-deleted
    
    Revisions have no `deletedAt` (no soft delete); the API delete and the revision purge cron
    remove rows. There are no migration files (TypeORM `synchronize` outside production), so an
    environment with existing data must run this **before** deploying, otherwise dropping the
    column brings soft-deleted rows back:
    
    ```sql
    DELETE FROM revisions WHERE "deletedAt" IS NOT NULL;
    ```
    
    ## Conventions
    
    - HTTP handlers extend the generated abstract class from
      `@notopia-uit/api-document-nestjs-server` — change `api/document/` and run `nx gen api`
      first, then implement the new method.
    - Kafka payload types come from `@notopia-uit/api-share-gen` (defined in `api/share/`),
      never hand-written interfaces.
    - `@Traceable()` on services; structured logger calls are `this.logger.log({...}, 'msg')`.
    
    ## Database schema and migrations
    
    No sync or migrate on startup (`synchronize: false`). Schema changes go through the TypeORM
    CLI via `nx run document:db:{sync,generate,create,migrate,revert,status}` (see `package.json`).
    `db:sync` is dev only and destructive; prod uses `db:migrate`. `just fixtures-document` runs
    `db:sync` first.
    # Note Service
    
    Workspaces, folders, notes, links, tags, trash, publishing. DDD + CQRS.
    Entrypoint: `cmd/note/`. HTTP spec: `api/note/`. gRPC: `proto/note/`.
    
    ## Layers
    
    | Dir | Contains | Rules |
    | --- | --- | --- |
    | `domain/` | Aggregates (`workspace`, `folder`, `note`), repo interfaces, `UnitOfWork` | No imports from `app`/`infra`. Pure |
    | `app/` | One file per use case + outbound service interfaces | Depends on `domain` interfaces only |
    | `infra/` | Adapters implementing `domain`/`app` interfaces | Where postgres/kafka/grpc/meili live |
    | `controller/` | `http/` (gin), `grpc/`, `event/`, `health/` | Thin — translate, don't decide |
    | `errs/` | Typed errors | Mapped to HTTP status in `controller/http/err.go` |
    
    ## Aggregate convention
    
    Unexported fields; a `NewX(...)` (validates, for creation) / `UnmarshalX(...)` (no
    validation, for rehydration from DB) pair; mutators take a trailing `userID string` and
    call `addEvent(...)`; `PopEvents()` drains. The repo `Save` is what publishes drained
    events. See `domain/note.go`.
    
    ## `app/` file naming
    
    | Prefix | Kind | Interface |
    | --- | --- | --- |
    | `cmd_*.go` | Write use case | `commonhandler.Cmd[T]` |
    | `q_*.go` | Read model query — bypasses aggregates, hits `pgreadmodel` | `commonhandler.Query[Q,R]` |
    | `e_*.go` | Event handler (domain event → integration event, or inbound) | — |
    | `svc_*.go` | Outbound service interface (implemented in `infra/service/`) | — |
    
    Writes go through `uow.Execute(ctx, func(r domain.RepoRegistry) error {...})`, which owns
    the transaction. Do not open transactions in handlers.
    
    ## Adding a use case
    
    1. Domain method + event in `domain/` if state changes shape
    2. `app/cmd_foo.go` — struct, `NewFooHandler`, `var ProvideFooHandler = NewFooHandler`,
       `type FooCmd commonhandler.Cmd[Foo]`, `var _ FooCmd = (*FooHandler)(nil)`
    3. Register in `app/wire.go` and `app/app.go` (the `Server` struct aggregating handlers)
    4. Path yaml in `api/note/paths/` + entry in `api/note/openapi.yaml`, then `nx gen api`
    5. Implement the generated method in `controller/http/`, map in `mapin.go`/`mapout.go`
    6. `nx wire note` if providers changed
    
    ## Persistence (`infra/persistence/`)
    
    - `pgmigration/*.sql` — goose. New migration = new numbered file, never edit an applied one
    - `pgsqlc/` — sqlc. Write the `.sql`, the `.sql.go` is generated alongside it
    - `pgrepo/` — aggregate repos (write side); `pgreadmodel/` — denormalized reads (`q_*`)
    
    ## Events
    
    `infra/outbox/` is a Watermill transactional outbox: integration events are written in the
    same transaction as the domain change, then forwarded to Redpanda. This is why
    `IntegrationPublisher.Publish` is safe to call inside `uow.Execute`.
    
    Published integration topics: `note.created`, `note.updated`, `note.deleted`,
    `workspace.deleted`. Every permanent delete (folder, note, trash) deletes the affected
    notes through the note repo first, so each one emits its own `NoteDeletedEvent`.
    
    `e_documentcommitted.go` is the inbound side — consumes the document service's commit event
    and updates note size, tags and outgoing links.
    
    ## Entitlement gates (billing)
    
    Billing calls (`app/svc_billing.go`) are uncached; unreachable billing → 503
    `billingServiceUnavailable`. 402 carries `PaymentRequiredError` with `requiredPlan` (cheapest
    tier that unlocks it); 409 `billingPayerMustTransfer`. Helpers in `app/billinggate.go`.
    
    - `members` limit (`UpdateWorkspaceMembers`): blocks growth only, so an over-limit workspace
      after a downgrade can still remove members or change roles.
    - Payer guard: the payer may not be demoted/removed/leave while billing says
      `requires_payer` (409); allowed for lifetime or cancelling subscriptions.
    - `UpdateWorkspaceMembers` checks owner/manage permission first, so 403 wins over 402/409.
    - `workspace_graph` feature → 402 when missing; note graph `depth` is clamped to the
      `note_graph_max_depth` limit (no error).
    - TODO: gate `published_notes` when publishing is implemented (`cmd_publishnote.go` and
      `cmd_publishworkspace.go` are stubs; the limit lives in billing).
    
    ## Crons
    
    `controller/cron/` registers `note:purge-expired-trash` (`PurgeExpiredTrashHandler`), env
    `NOTOPIA_NOTE_CRON_PURGE_EXPIRED_TRASH_{NAME,SCHEDULE,TIMEOUT,ENABLED}`, default `0 3 * * *`,
    runs with `time.Local`, locked via `pkgcron.Locker`. Per workspace the cutoff is the plan's
    `trash_retention_days`, but never younger than 24h (`purgeMinTrashAge`); unlimited retention
    and workspaces missing from the entitlements result are skipped (warn). Billing down → batch
    skipped. Runs as the service-account user.
    
    ## Redis
    
    `infra/common` owns the single Redis client, shared by the SSE hub (`workspaceevent`,
    Redis streams) and the cron locker. Billing changes arrive as an event (`e_billingchanged.go`)
    and are published to the workspace SSE channel as `WorkspaceBillingChangedEvent`
    `{workspaceId, plan}`.
    
    ## Gotchas
    
    - Trash read-model filters compare `trashed_by::text = sqlc.narg('trashed_by')::text` (the
      cast is needed for the nullable arg); keep it when editing those queries.
    - `cmd_createworkspace.go` calls `authorizationSvc.CreateWorkspaceWithOwner` *inside*
      `uow.Execute` — a known cross-service side effect that can diverge if the commit fails
      (see the TODO there). Don't copy this pattern into new code; use the outbox.
    - `q_workspacesearchtoken.go` mints scoped Meilisearch tenant tokens — search scoping is
      decided here, not in `search-worker`.
    # lib-server (`@notopia-uit/lib-server`)
    
    Node-only shared code for NestJS services.
    
    | Entry | Contents |
    | --- | --- |
    | `./block-note` | BlockNote server schema (`createSchema`) |
    | `./locks` | `LocksSetupModule.forRoot({ redisUrl?, ttl? })` over `@nestjs/locks`, `RedisLockStore` |
    
    ## Locks
    
    - With `redisUrl`, locks use `RedisLockStore`. That Redis must run with `noeviction` and
      persistence, and the app must call `app.enableShutdownHooks()`.
    - Without `redisUrl`, an in-memory store is used and a warning is logged. **This is
      intended, also in production**: it keeps single-instance deployments and local
      development free of an extra Redis. Do not turn it into a startup error. Running more
      than one instance without `redisUrl` lets every instance run the same cron.

    import { type ClientGrpc } from '@nestjs/microservices';
    import {

    const unavailableCodes: number[] = [status.UNAVAILABLE, status.DEADLINE_EXCEEDED];
    
    export const toPlanTier = (tier: PlanTierPb): PlanTier => {
      switch (tier) {
        case PlanTierPb.PLAN_TIER_FREE:
          return PlanTier.Free;
        case PlanTierPb.PLAN_TIER_PLUS:
          return PlanTier.Plus;
        case PlanTierPb.PLAN_TIER_PRO:
          return PlanTier.Pro;
        default:
          throw new InternalServerErrorException(`Invalid plan tier from billing: ${tier}`);
      }
    };
    
    const toNumber = (value: unknown): number => {
      if (typeof value === 'object' && value !== null && 'toNumber' in value) {
        return (value as { toNumber(): number }).toNumber();
      }
      return Number(value);
    };
    
    const pickKnown = <K extends string, V>(
      known: readonly K[],
      raw: Record<string, unknown> | undefined,
      map: (value: unknown) => V
    ): Partial<Record<K, V>> => {
      const out: Partial<Record<K, V>> = {};
      for (const key of known) {
        if (raw && Object.hasOwn(raw, key)) {
          out[key] = map(raw[key]);
        }
      }
      return out;
    };
    
    export const toFeatures = (raw: Record<string, unknown> | undefined) =>
      pickKnown(Object.values(PlanFeature), raw, Boolean);
    
    export const toLimits = (raw: Record<string, unknown> | undefined) =>
      pickKnown(Object.values(PlanLimit), raw, toNumber);
    
    export const toEntitlements = (e: EntitlementsPb | undefined): Entitlements => {
      if (!e) {
        throw new InternalServerErrorException('Missing entitlements from billing');
      }
      return { plan: toPlanTier(e.plan), features: toFeatures(e.features), limits: toLimits(e.limits) };
    };
    
    @Injectable()
    @Traceable()
    export class BillingService implements OnModuleInit {
      private static readonly batchGetEntitlementsLimit = 500;
      private billingServiceClient!: BillingServiceClient;
    
      constructor(@Inject(BILLING_PACKAGE_NAME) private readonly client: ClientGrpc) {}
    
      onModuleInit(): void {
        this.billingServiceClient = this.client.getService<BillingServiceClient>(BILLING_SERVICE_NAME);
      }
    
      private async call<T>(request: Observable<T>): Promise<T> {
        try {
          return await firstValueFrom(request);
        } catch (error) {
          if (isGrpcError(error) && error.code !== undefined && unavailableCodes.includes(error.code)) {
            throw new BillingUnavailableException(error);
          }
          throw error;
        }
      }
    
      async getEntitlements(workspaceId: string): Promise<Entitlements> {
        const response = await this.call(
          this.billingServiceClient.getWorkspaceEntitlements({ workspaceId })
        );
        return toEntitlements(response.entitlements);
      }
    
      async batchGetEntitlements(workspaceIds: string[]): Promise<Map<string, Entitlements>> {
        const out = new Map<string, Entitlements>();
        const chunkSize = BillingService.batchGetEntitlementsLimit;
        for (let i = 0; i < workspaceIds.length; i += chunkSize) {
          const response = await this.call(
            this.billingServiceClient.batchGetWorkspaceEntitlements({
              workspaceIds: workspaceIds.slice(i, i + chunkSize),
            })
          );
          for (const [id, entitlements] of Object.entries(response.entitlements)) {
            out.set(id, toEntitlements(entitlements));
          }
        }
        return out;
      }
    
      async listPlans(): Promise<PlanEntitlements[]> {
        const response = await this.call(this.billingServiceClient.listPlans({}));
        return response.plans.map((plan) => ({
          tier: toPlanTier(plan.tier),
          features: toFeatures(plan.features),
          limits: toLimits(plan.limits),
        }));
      }
    }

    type PlanTier uint8
    
    const (
        PlanTierUnspecified PlanTier = iota
        PlanTierFree
        PlanTierPlus
        PlanTierPro
    )
    
    func (t PlanTier) IsValid() bool {
        switch t {
        case PlanTierUnspecified, PlanTierFree, PlanTierPlus, PlanTierPro:
            return true
        default:
            return false
        }
    }
    
    func (t PlanTier) String() string {
        switch t {
        case PlanTierFree:
            return "free"
        case PlanTierPlus:
            return "plus"
        case PlanTierPro:
            return "pro"
        case PlanTierUnspecified:
            return "unspecified"
        default:
            return "unknown"
        }
    }
    
    type PlanFeature uint8
    
    const (

        PlanFeatureWorkspaceGraph
    )
    
    func (f PlanFeature) IsValid() bool {
        switch f {
        case PlanFeatureUnspecified, PlanFeatureWorkspaceGraph:
            return true
        default:
            return false
        }
    }
    
    func (f PlanFeature) String() string {
        switch f {
        case PlanFeatureWorkspaceGraph:
            return "workspace_graph"
        case PlanFeatureUnspecified:
            return "unspecified"
        default:
            return "unknown"
        }
    }
    
    func ParsePlanFeature(s string) (PlanFeature, bool) {
        switch s {
        case PlanFeatureWorkspaceGraph.String():
            return PlanFeatureWorkspaceGraph, true
        default:
            return PlanFeatureUnspecified, false
        }
    }
    
    type PlanLimit uint8
    
    const (
        PlanLimitUnspecified PlanLimit = iota
        PlanLimitMembers
        PlanLimitNoteGraphMaxDepth
        PlanLimitTrashRetentionDays
    )
    
    func (l PlanLimit) IsValid() bool {
        switch l {
        case PlanLimitUnspecified,
            PlanLimitMembers,
            PlanLimitNoteGraphMaxDepth,
            PlanLimitTrashRetentionDays:
            return true
        default:
            return false
        }
    }
    
    func (l PlanLimit) String() string {
        switch l {
        case PlanLimitMembers:
            return "members"
        case PlanLimitNoteGraphMaxDepth:
            return "note_graph_max_depth"
        case PlanLimitTrashRetentionDays:
            return "trash_retention_days"
        case PlanLimitUnspecified:
            return "unspecified"
        default:
            return "unknown"
        }
    }
    
    func ParsePlanLimit(s string) (PlanLimit, bool) {
        switch s {
        case PlanLimitMembers.String():
            return PlanLimitMembers, true
        case PlanLimitNoteGraphMaxDepth.String():
            return PlanLimitNoteGraphMaxDepth, true
        case PlanLimitTrashRetentionDays.String():
            return PlanLimitTrashRetentionDays, true
        default:
            return PlanLimitUnspecified, false
        }
    }
    
    type PlanQuota int64
    
    const PlanQuotaUnlimited PlanQuota = -1
    
    func (q PlanQuota) IsUnlimited() bool { return q == PlanQuotaUnlimited }
    
    func (q PlanQuota) Allows(n int64) bool { return q.IsUnlimited() || n <= int64(q) }
    
    type Entitlements struct {
        Plan     PlanTier
        Features map[PlanFeature]bool
        Limits   map[PlanLimit]PlanQuota
    }
    
    func (e Entitlements) Feature(f PlanFeature) bool { return e.Features[f] }
    
    func (e Entitlements) Limit(l PlanLimit) PlanQuota { return e.Limits[l] }
    
    type PlanEntitlements struct {
        Tier     PlanTier
        Features map[PlanFeature]bool
        Limits   map[PlanLimit]PlanQuota
    }
    
    var paidTiers = []PlanTier{PlanTierPlus, PlanTierPro}
    
    func planByTier(plans []PlanEntitlements, tier PlanTier) (PlanEntitlements, bool) {
        for _, p := range plans {
            if p.Tier == tier {
                return p, true
            }
        }
        return PlanEntitlements{}, false
    }
    
    func RequiredPlanForFeature(plans []PlanEntitlements, f PlanFeature) PlanTier {
        for _, tier := range paidTiers {
            if p, ok := planByTier(plans, tier); ok && p.Features[f] {
                return tier
            }
        }
        return PlanTierPro
    }
    
    func RequiredPlanForLimit(plans []PlanEntitlements, l PlanLimit, needed int64) PlanTier {
        for _, tier := range paidTiers {
            if p, ok := planByTier(plans, tier); ok && p.Limits[l].Allows(needed) {
                return tier
            }
        }
        return PlanTierPro
    }

    package domain
    
    import (
        "fmt"
        "maps"
        "time"
    
        "github.com/notopia-uit/notopia/internal/billing/errs"
    )
    
    type Plan struct {
        eventRecorder
        tier      PlanTier
        features  map[FeatureKey]bool
        limits    map[LimitKey]int64
        updatedAt time.Time
    }
    
    func NewPlan(tier PlanTier, features map[FeatureKey]bool, limits map[LimitKey]int64, now time.Time) (*Plan, error) {
        p := &Plan{
            eventRecorder: eventRecorder{events: nil},
            tier:          tier,
            features:      map[FeatureKey]bool{},
            limits:        map[LimitKey]int64{},
            updatedAt:     now,
        }
        if !tier.IsValid() {
            return nil, errs.NewInvalid(fmt.Sprintf("invalid tier %q", tier))
        }
        if err := p.apply(features, limits); err != nil {
            return nil, err
        }
        for _, k := range FeatureKeys {
            if _, ok := p.features[k]; !ok {
                p.features[k] = false
            }
        }
        for _, k := range LimitKeys {
            if _, ok := p.limits[k]; !ok {
                p.limits[k] = 0
            }
        }
        return p, nil
    }
    
    func UnmarshalPlan(tier PlanTier, features map[FeatureKey]bool, limits map[LimitKey]int64, updatedAt time.Time) *Plan {
        return &Plan{
            eventRecorder: eventRecorder{events: nil},
            tier:          tier,
            features:      features,
            limits:        limits,
            updatedAt:     updatedAt,
        }
    }
    
    func (p *Plan) apply(features map[FeatureKey]bool, limits map[LimitKey]int64) error {
        for k, v := range features {
            if !k.IsValid() {
                return errs.NewInvalid(fmt.Sprintf("unknown feature %q", k))
            }
            p.features[k] = v
        }
        for k, v := range limits {
            if !k.IsValid() {
                return errs.NewInvalid(fmt.Sprintf("unknown limit %q", k))
            }
            if v < Unlimited {
                return errs.NewInvalid(fmt.Sprintf("limit %q must be >= -1", k))
            }
            p.limits[k] = v
        }
        return nil
    }
    
    func (p *Plan) Update(features map[FeatureKey]bool, limits map[LimitKey]int64, now time.Time, userID string) error {
        if err := p.apply(features, limits); err != nil {
            return err
        }
        p.updatedAt = now
        p.record(&PlanUpdatedEvent{BaseEvent: NewBaseEvent(p.tier.String(), userID), Features: features, Limits: limits})
        return nil
    }
    
    func (p *Plan) Tier() PlanTier                { return p.tier }
    func (p *Plan) Feature(k FeatureKey) bool     { return p.features[k] }
    func (p *Plan) Limit(k LimitKey) int64        { return p.limits[k] }
    func (p *Plan) Features() map[FeatureKey]bool { return maps.Clone(p.features) }
    func (p *Plan) Limits() map[LimitKey]int64    { return maps.Clone(p.limits) }
    func (p *Plan) UpdatedAt() time.Time          { return p.updatedAt }
    
    func DefaultPlans(now time.Time) []*Plan {
        mk := func(t PlanTier, autoCommit, graph bool, members, published, depth, interval, revisions, trash, ai int64) *Plan {
            p, _ := NewPlan(t,
                map[FeatureKey]bool{FeatureKeyAutoCommit: autoCommit, FeatureKeyWorkspaceGraph: graph},
                map[LimitKey]int64{
                    LimitKeyMembers: members, LimitKeyPublishedNotes: published, LimitKeyNoteGraphMaxDepth: depth,
                    LimitKeyAutoCommitMinInterval: interval, LimitKeyRevisionHistoryDays: revisions,
                    LimitKeyTrashRetentionDays: trash, LimitKeyAICreditsMonthly: ai,
                }, now)
            return p
        }
        return []*Plan{
            mk(PlanTierFree, false, false, 3, 3, 5, 0, 7, 7, 0),
            mk(PlanTierPlus, true, true, 10, Unlimited, Unlimited, 300, 30, 30, 200),
            mk(PlanTierPro, true, true, Unlimited, Unlimited, Unlimited, 60, Unlimited, 90, 2000),
        }
    }

          const result = await this.meili.index(SearchService.noteIndex).search(query, {
            filter: workspaceId ? `workspaceId = "${workspaceId}"` : undefined,
            limit,
          });
          return result.hits.map((hit) => ({
            id: String(hit.id),
            name: String(hit.name ?? ''),
            folderId: hit.folderId as string | undefined,
            folderName: hit.folderName as string | undefined,
            tags: hit.tags as string[] | undefined,
          }));
        } catch (error) {
          this.logger.error({ err: error, query }, 'Failed to search notes');
          throw error;
        }
      }
    }

      private client!: AuthorizationServiceClient;
    
      constructor(@Inject(AUTHORIZATION_PACKAGE_NAME) private readonly grpc: ClientGrpc) {}

        this.client = this.grpc.getService<AuthorizationServiceClient>(AUTHORIZATION_SERVICE_NAME);
      }
    
      async getUserWorkspaces({ userId }: { userId: string }): Promise<WorkspaceSummary[]> {
        this.logger.debug('Fetching user workspaces for tool call');

        return response.workspaces.map((workspace) => ({
          workspaceId: workspace.id,
          role: String(workspace.role),
        }));
      }
    }

## Assistant

The merge changes the plan: **billing already owns subscriptions and exposes the AI quota we need.** We can integrate entirely from the AI service.

I checked the billing implementation, gRPC contract, and note/document enforcement:

- Billing exposes `GetWorkspaceEntitlements` and `ListPlans`.
- The existing limit is **`ai_credits_monthly`**, with default quotas of Free **0**, Plus **200**, Pro **2,000**. Runtime checks must use billing’s values.
- The [enforcement design](/home/ntgnguyen/Projects/notopia/docs/superpowers/specs/2026-10-11-billing-04-enforcement-design.md:206) explicitly assigns AI usage counting to the AI service.
- Consumers fetch entitlements without caching; subscription events are best-effort notifications.
- Document now supports plan-gated automatic commits. My earlier statement that commits were manual-only is outdated.

The revised scope is **AI backend only**: no changes to billing, note, document, shared contracts, or UI.

1. **Secure the existing AI tools**
   - Fix search authorization before adding tools.
   - Scope searches to authorized workspaces and exclude trashed notes.
   - Validate requests and tool inputs at runtime.
   - Preserve automatic tool selection.

2. **Connect AI to existing billing gRPC**
   - Add an AI-local billing client using the generated contract.
   - Authorize workspace access before fetching entitlements.
   - Read `ai_credits_monthly` on each generation request.
   - Return `402` for unavailable/exhausted credits and `503` when billing is unreachable.
   - Keep subscription status interpretation inside billing; consume its resolved entitlements.

3. **Implement AI-owned usage accounting**
   - Atomically reserve credits before generation so concurrent requests cannot overspend.
   - Use Redis for shared counters, reservations, and throttling.
   - Make accounting idempotent across retries and tool continuations.
   - Record generation usage for observability.

   **Proposed initial policy:** one credit per assistant generation, including its server-side tool steps, against a workspace’s UTC calendar-month allowance. This is a proposal: the current contract defines neither credit cost nor quota reset dates. Redis-backed accounting also needs persistence; it must not silently fall back to memory for paid quota enforcement.

4. **Add throttling and stream lifecycle handling**
   - Per-user request and concurrent-stream limits; optional trusted client-IP limits.
   - Configurable timeouts, output limits, and maximum tool steps.
   - Cancel generation on disconnect and settle reservations according to the accounting policy.
   - Normalize HTTP, stream, and tool failures within the AI backend.

5. **Provide tools dynamically using existing interfaces**

   | Tool | Planned behavior |
   |---|---|
   | `listWorkspaces` | Discover accessible workspaces |
   | `searchNotes` | Authorized search with bounded excerpts |
   | `getNote` | Existing permission-checked metadata lookup |
   | `getNoteWorkspace` | Use existing user-aware note gRPC lookup |
   | `readIndexedNoteContent` | Read authorized, committed search content; explicitly identify it as potentially stale |

   Tool availability will depend on request context and permissions, with checks repeated during execution. Workspace billing context must be explicit and validated; the model must not choose which workspace pays.

6. **Verify and update AI-local documentation**
   - Test cross-workspace access, concurrent quota reservations, duplicate requests, billing outages, throttling, and stream failures.
   - Run AI lint/typechecks and update its stale guidance.

Full live-document reading, workspace tree/graph tools, editor manipulation, sidebar UI, URL context, and commit-button changes are deferred. They need interfaces or frontend changes outside this scope. Existing client-supplied BlockNote editing tools will remain supported.

One integration constraint remains: current clients do not send a dedicated billing workspace field. The AI backend can add support now, but existing clients need a compatible way to identify the workspace before workspace credit enforcement can work end to end.

    func toGRPCError(err error) error {
        if cerr, ok := errors.AsType[errs.Error](err); ok {
            switch cerr.Code() {
            case errs.CodeUnauthorized:
                return status.Error(codes.Unauthenticated, cerr.Error())
            case errs.CodeForbidden, errs.CodeNotOwner:
                return status.Error(codes.PermissionDenied, cerr.Error())
            case errs.CodeInvalid:
                return status.Error(codes.InvalidArgument, cerr.Error())
            case errs.CodeNotFound, errs.CodeNoBillingAccount:
                return status.Error(codes.NotFound, cerr.Error())
            case errs.CodeSubscriptionAlreadyActive,
                errs.CodeNoActiveSubscription,
                errs.CodeRefundWindowExpired,
                errs.CodeAlreadyPayer,
                errs.CodePriceNotActive:
                return status.Error(codes.FailedPrecondition, cerr.Error())
            case errs.CodeWebhookSignature:
                return status.Error(codes.InvalidArgument, cerr.Error())
            case errs.CodeInternal, errs.CodePaymentProvider, errs.CodeAuthorizationService:
                return status.Error(codes.Internal, cerr.Error())
            default:
                return status.Error(codes.Internal, cerr.Error())
            }
        }
        return err
    }
    
    func unaryErrorInterceptor(
        ctx context.Context,
        req any,
        info *grpc.UnaryServerInfo,
        handler grpc.UnaryHandler,
    ) (any, error) {
        resp, err := handler(ctx, req)
        if err != nil {
            return nil, toGRPCError(err)
        }
        return resp, nil
    }

        }

                    logging.StartCall,
                    logging.FinishCall,
                    logging.PayloadSent,
                    logging.PayloadReceived,
                )),

                unaryErrorInterceptor,
            ),

        }

    }

        "google.golang.org/protobuf/types/known/timestamppb"
    )
    
    func toPBPlanTier(t app.PlanTier) (pb.PlanTier, error) {
        switch t {
        case app.PlanTierFree:
            return pb.PlanTier_PLAN_TIER_FREE, nil
        case app.PlanTierPlus:
            return pb.PlanTier_PLAN_TIER_PLUS, nil
        case app.PlanTierPro:
            return pb.PlanTier_PLAN_TIER_PRO, nil
        case app.PlanTierUnspecified:
        }
        return pb.PlanTier_PLAN_TIER_UNSPECIFIED, errs.NewInternal(fmt.Sprintf("invalid plan tier: %v", t), nil)
    }
    
    func toPBStatus(s app.SubscriptionStatus) (pb.SubscriptionStatus, error) {
        switch s {
        case app.SubscriptionStatusNone:
            return pb.SubscriptionStatus_SUBSCRIPTION_STATUS_NONE, nil
        case app.SubscriptionStatusIncomplete:
            return pb.SubscriptionStatus_SUBSCRIPTION_STATUS_INCOMPLETE, nil
        case app.SubscriptionStatusActive:
            return pb.SubscriptionStatus_SUBSCRIPTION_STATUS_ACTIVE, nil
        case app.SubscriptionStatusPastDue:
            return pb.SubscriptionStatus_SUBSCRIPTION_STATUS_PAST_DUE, nil
        case app.SubscriptionStatusUnpaid:
            return pb.SubscriptionStatus_SUBSCRIPTION_STATUS_UNPAID, nil
        case app.SubscriptionStatusCanceled:
            return pb.SubscriptionStatus_SUBSCRIPTION_STATUS_CANCELED, nil
        case app.SubscriptionStatusIncompleteExpired:
            return pb.SubscriptionStatus_SUBSCRIPTION_STATUS_INCOMPLETE_EXPIRED, nil
        default:
            return pb.SubscriptionStatus_SUBSCRIPTION_STATUS_UNSPECIFIED, errs.NewInternal(fmt.Sprintf("invalid subscription status: %v", s), nil)
        }
    }
    
    func toPBEntitlements(e app.Entitlements) (*pb.Entitlements, error) {
        plan, err := toPBPlanTier(e.Plan)
        if err != nil {
            return nil, err
        }
        status, err := toPBStatus(e.Status)
        if err != nil {
            return nil, err
        }
        out := &pb.Entitlements{
            WorkspaceId: e.WorkspaceID.String(), Plan: plan, Status: status,
            Features: e.Features, Limits: e.Limits, AccessUntil: nil,
        }
        if e.AccessUntil != nil {
            out.AccessUntil = timestamppb.New(*e.AccessUntil)
        }
        return out, nil
    }

    import (

        "github.com/google/uuid"

        "github.com/notopia-uit/notopia/internal/billing/errs"
        "github.com/notopia-uit/notopia/pkg/pb"
    )
    
    func parseUUID(s string) (uuid.UUID, error) {
        id, err := uuid.Parse(s)
        if err != nil {
            return uuid.Nil, errs.NewInvalid("invalid uuid: " + s)
        }
        return id, nil
    }
    
    func (s *ServiceServer) GetWorkspaceEntitlements(ctx context.Context, req *pb.GetWorkspaceEntitlementsRequest) (*pb.GetWorkspaceEntitlementsResponse, error) {
        id, err := parseUUID(req.WorkspaceId)
        if err != nil {
            return nil, err
        }
        ent, err := s.app.Queries.GetEntitlements.Handle(ctx, &app.GetEntitlements{WorkspaceID: id, UserID: "", Internal: true})
        if err != nil {
            return nil, err
        }
        out, err := toPBEntitlements(ent)
        if err != nil {
            return nil, err
        }
        return &pb.GetWorkspaceEntitlementsResponse{Entitlements: out}, nil
    }
    
    func (s *ServiceServer) BatchGetWorkspaceEntitlements(ctx context.Context, req *pb.BatchGetWorkspaceEntitlementsRequest) (*pb.BatchGetWorkspaceEntitlementsResponse, error) {
        ids := make([]uuid.UUID, 0, len(req.WorkspaceIds))
        for _, raw := range req.WorkspaceIds {
            id, err := parseUUID(raw)
            if err != nil {
                return nil, err
            }
            ids = append(ids, id)
        }
        res, err := s.app.Queries.BatchGetEntitlements.Handle(ctx, &app.BatchGetEntitlements{WorkspaceIDs: ids})
        if err != nil {
            return nil, err
        }
        out := make(map[string]*pb.Entitlements, len(res))
        for id, e := range res {
            if out[id.String()], err = toPBEntitlements(e); err != nil {
                return nil, err
            }
        }
        return &pb.BatchGetWorkspaceEntitlementsResponse{Entitlements: out}, nil
    }
    
    func (s *ServiceServer) GetWorkspacePayer(ctx context.Context, req *pb.GetWorkspacePayerRequest) (*pb.GetWorkspacePayerResponse, error) {
        id, err := parseUUID(req.WorkspaceId)
        if err != nil {
            return nil, err
        }
        v, err := s.app.Queries.GetWorkspacePayer.Handle(ctx, &app.GetWorkspacePayer{WorkspaceID: id})
        if err != nil {
            return nil, err
        }
        return &pb.GetWorkspacePayerResponse{PayerId: v.PayerID, RequiresPayer: v.RequiresPayer}, nil
    }
    
    func (s *ServiceServer) ListPlans(ctx context.Context, _ *pb.ListPlansRequest) (*pb.ListPlansResponse, error) {
        views, err := s.app.Queries.ListPlans.Handle(ctx, &app.ListPlans{})
        if err != nil {
            return nil, err
        }
        out := &pb.ListPlansResponse{}
        for _, v := range views {
            tier, err := toPBPlanTier(v.Plan.Tier)
            if err != nil {
                return nil, err
            }
            out.Plans = append(out.Plans, &pb.BillingPlan{Tier: tier, Features: v.Plan.Features, Limits: v.Plan.Limits})
        }
        return out, nil
    }

    ### lazyConnect, enableOfflineQueue, connectTimeout options
    
    Source: https://github.com/redis/ioredis/blob/main/lib/redis/RedisOptions.ts
    
    `lazyConnect` delays connection until the first command (or explicit `.connect()`). `enableOfflineQueue` buffers commands when the stream isn't writable. `connectTimeout` (default 10000ms) kills the socket on inactivity during initial connection. `maxRetriesPerRequest` limits offline queue retries before flushing with error.
    
    ```typescript
      /**
       * How long the client will wait before killing a socket due to inactivity during initial connection.
       * @default 10000
       */
      connectTimeout?: number | undefined;
    
      /**
       * @default 20
       */
      maxRetriesPerRequest?: number | null | undefined;
    
      offlineQueue?: boolean | undefined;
      commandQueue?: boolean | undefined;
    
      /**
       * By default, if the connection to Redis server has not been established, commands are added to a queue
       * and are executed once the connection is "ready"... If this option is false, when execute the command
       * when the connection isn't ready, an error will be returned.
       * @default true
       */
      enableOfflineQueue?: boolean | undefined;
    
      /**
       * When a Redis instance is initialized, a connection to the server is immediately established. Set this to
       * true will delay the connection to the server until the first command is sent or `redis.connect()` is called
       * explicitly.
       * @default false
       */
      lazyConnect?: boolean | undefined;
    ```
    
    --------------------------------
    
    ### Set maxRetriesPerRequest to 1
    
    Source: https://github.com/redis/ioredis/blob/main/README.md
    
    Configures ioredis to flush pending commands with an error after 1 retry attempt. Setting maxRetriesPerRequest to null disables this behavior, causing commands to wait indefinitely until the connection is restored.
    
    ```javascript
    const redis = new Redis({
      maxRetriesPerRequest: 1,
    });
    ```
    
    --------------------------------
    
    ### CommonRedisOptions > enableOfflineQueue
    
    Source: https://github.com/redis/ioredis/blob/main/docs/interfaces/CommonRedisOptions.html
    
    ### `Optional` enableOfflineQueue[](#enableOfflineQueue)
    
    enableOfflineQueue?: boolean
    
    By default, if the connection to Redis server has not been established, commands are added to a queue and are executed once the connection is "ready" (when `enableReadyCheck` is true, "ready" means the Redis server has loaded the database from disk, otherwise means the connection to the Redis server has been established). If this option is false, when execute the command when the connection isn't ready, an error will be returned.
    
    #### Default
    
    ```
    true
    Copy
    ```

    --------------------------------
    
    ### Disable Offline Queue
    
    Source: https://github.com/redis/ioredis/blob/main/README.md
    
    Set enableOfflineQueue to false to prevent commands from being queued when the connection is not ready.
    
    ```javascript
    const redis = new Redis({ enableOfflineQueue: false });
    ```

    ### CommonRedisOptions > lazyConnect
    
    Source: https://github.com/redis/ioredis/blob/main/docs/interfaces/CommonRedisOptions.html
    
    ### `Optional` lazyConnect[](#lazyConnect)
    
    lazyConnect?: boolean
    
    When a Redis instance is initialized, a connection to the server is immediately established. Set this to true will delay the connection to the server until the first command is sent or `redis.connect()` is called explicitly. When `redis.connect()` is called explicitly, a Promise is returned, which will be resolved when the connection is ready or rejected when it fails. The rejection should be handled by the user.

    ### Client
    
    Source: https://github.com/nestjs/docs.nestjs.com/blob/master/content/microservices/grpc.md
    
    Once registered, inject the configured `ClientGrpc` object with `@Inject()`. Then use the `ClientGrpc` object's `getService()` method to retrieve the service instance, as shown below.
    
    > error **Warning** The gRPC client does not send fields that contain an underscore (`_`) in their names unless the `keepCase` option is set to `true` in the proto loader configuration (`options.loader.keepCase` in the microservice transporter configuration).
    
    This differs slightly from the technique used with other microservice transporters. Instead of the `ClientProxy` class, you use the `ClientGrpc` class, which provides the `getService()` method. The generic `getService()` method takes a service name as an argument and returns its instance (if available).
    
    --------------------------------
    
    ### Inject and obtain gRPC service proxy with @Inject
    
    Source: https://github.com/nestjs/docs.nestjs.com/blob/master/content/microservices/grpc.md
    
    Injects the configured ClientGrpc instance and retrieves the gRPC service proxy within onModuleInit(). Note that fields with underscores require keepCase: true in loader options.
    
    ```typescript
    @Injectable()
    export class AppService implements OnModuleInit {
      private heroesService: HeroesService;
    
      constructor(@Inject('HERO_PACKAGE') private client: ClientGrpc) {}
    
      onModuleInit() {
        this.heroesService = this.client.getService<HeroesService>('HeroesService');
      }
    
      getHero(): Observable<string> {
        return this.heroesService.findOne({ id: 1 });
      }
    }
    ```
    
    --------------------------------
    
    ### Handling timeouts
    
    Source: https://github.com/nestjs/docs.nestjs.com/blob/master/content/microservices/basics.md
    
    In distributed systems, microservices are sometimes down or unavailable. To avoid waiting indefinitely, apply a timeout to your microservice calls with the [RxJS](https://rxjs.dev) `timeout` operator. If the microservice doesn't respond within the specified time, an error is thrown, which you can catch and handle appropriately.
    
    Apply the `timeout` operator within the pipe:
    
    > info **Hint** The `timeout` operator is imported from the `rxjs/operators` package.
    
    If the microservice doesn't respond within 5 seconds, the `Observable` errors with a `TimeoutError`.
    
    --------------------------------
    
    ### TimeoutInterceptor with RxJS timeout and catchError
    
    Source: https://github.com/nestjs/docs.nestjs.com/blob/master/content/interceptors.md
    
    Uses timeout(5000) to fail the stream with TimeoutError if the handler doesn't emit within 5 seconds, then maps it to RequestTimeoutException. Unsubscribing does not abort handler work, so add custom cleanup if needed. The example is shown in TypeScript and JavaScript (switch) variants.
    
    ```typescript
    import { Injectable, NestInterceptor, ExecutionContext, CallHandler, RequestTimeoutException } from '@nestjs/common';
    import { Observable, throwError, TimeoutError } from 'rxjs';
    import { catchError, timeout } from 'rxjs/operators';
    
    @Injectable()
    export class TimeoutInterceptor implements NestInterceptor {
      intercept(context: ExecutionContext, next: CallHandler): Observable<any> {
        return next.handle().pipe(
          timeout(5000),
          catchError(err => {
            if (err instanceof TimeoutError) {
              return throwError(() => new RequestTimeoutException());
            }
            return throwError(() => err);
          }),
        );
      }
    }
    ```
    
    ```javascript
    import { Injectable, RequestTimeoutException } from '@nestjs/common';
    import { throwError, TimeoutError } from 'rxjs';
    import { catchError, timeout } from 'rxjs/operators';
    
    @Injectable()
    export class TimeoutInterceptor {
      intercept(context, next) {
        return next.handle().pipe(
          timeout(5000),
          catchError(err => {
            if (err instanceof TimeoutError) {
              return throwError(() => new RequestTimeoutException());
            }
            return throwError(() => err);
          }),
        );
      }
    }
    ```
    
    --------------------------------
    
    ### Apply timeout to microservice calls with RxJS timeout operator
    
    Source: https://github.com/nestjs/docs.nestjs.com/blob/master/content/microservices/basics.md
    
    Use the timeout operator within the pipe to limit waiting time for microservice responses. If the microservice doesn't respond within 5 seconds, the Observable errors with a TimeoutError. The timeout operator is imported from rxjs/operators.
    
    ```typescript
    this.client
      .send<TResult, TInput>(pattern, data)
      .pipe(timeout(5000));
    ```

    ### Handle streamText errors with onError in toUIMessageStream
    
    Source: https://ai-sdk.dev/docs/ai-sdk-core/tools-and-tool-calling
    
    When using streamText with toUIMessageStream, pass an onError function to return custom error messages for NoSuchToolError and InvalidToolInputError. Other errors return a generic message.
    
    ```typescript
    const result = streamText({
      // ...
    });
    
    return createUIMessageStreamResponse({
      stream: toUIMessageStream({
        stream: result.stream,
        onError: error => {
          if (NoSuchToolError.isInstance(error)) {
            return 'The model tried to call a unknown tool.';
          } else if (InvalidToolInputError.isInstance(error)) {
            return 'The model called a tool with invalid inputs.';
          } else {
            return 'An unknown error occurred.';
          }
        },
      }),
    });
    ```

    Source: https://ai-sdk.dev/docs/migration-guides/migration-guide-5-0

    ### Validate messages with tools using validateUIMessages in API route
    
    Source: https://ai-sdk.dev/docs/ai-sdk-ui/chatbot-message-persistence
    
    Validates loaded messages against tool definitions, data schemas, and metadata schema before streaming. Use this in a POST handler when messages include tool calls, custom metadata, or data parts.
    
    ```typescript
    import {
      convertToModelMessages,
      createUIMessageStreamResponse,
      streamText,
      toUIMessageStream,
      UIMessage,
      validateUIMessages,
      tool,
    } from 'ai';
    import { z } from 'zod';
    import { loadChat, saveChat } from '@util/chat-store';
    import { dataSchemas, metadataSchema } from '@util/schemas';
    
    // Define your tools
    const tools = {
      weather: tool({
        description: 'Get weather information',
        inputSchema: z.object({
          location: z.string(),
          units: z.enum(['celsius', 'fahrenheit']),
        }),
        execute: async ({ location, units }) => {
          /* tool implementation */
        },
      }),
      // other tools
    };
    
    export async function POST(req: Request) {
      const { message, id } = await req.json();
    
      // Load previous messages from database
      const previousMessages = await loadChat(id);
    
      // Append new message to previousMessages messages
      const messages = [...previousMessages, message];
    
      // Validate loaded messages against
      // tools, data parts schema, and metadata schema
      const validatedMessages = await validateUIMessages({
        messages,
        tools, // Ensures tool calls in messages match current schemas
        dataSchemas,
        metadataSchema,
      });
    
      const result = streamText({
        model: 'openai/gpt-6-luna',
        messages: await convertToModelMessages(validatedMessages),
        tools,
      });
    
      return createUIMessageStreamResponse({
        stream: toUIMessageStream({
          stream: result.stream,
          originalMessages: messages,
          onEnd: ({ messages }) => {
            saveChat({ chatId: id, messages });
          },
        }),
      });
    }
    ```
    
    --------------------------------
    
    ### Forward req.signal as abortSignal to streamText in chat route
    
    Source: https://ai-sdk.dev/docs/advanced/vercel-deployment-guide
    
    Pass the route's req.signal to streamText as abortSignal so client cancellation reaches the model request. Requires the Node.js runtime (default for Next.js route handlers) and supportsCancellation enabled in vercel.json.
    
    ```typescript
    import { convertToModelMessages, streamText, type UIMessage } from 'ai';
    
    export async function POST(req: Request) {
      const { messages }: { messages: UIMessage[] } = await req.json();
    
      const result = streamText({
        model: "anthropic/claude-sonnet-5.5",
        messages: convertToModelMessages(messages),
        abortSignal: req.signal,
      });
    
      return result.toUIMessageStreamResponse();
    }
    ```
    
    --------------------------------
    
    ### Handle abort in toUIMessageStream with consumeStream in createUIMessageStreamResponse
    
    Source: https://ai-sdk.dev/docs/advanced/stopping-streams
    
    Use this POST handler pattern when streaming UI messages and needing abort-aware cleanup. Pass consumeStream as consumeSseStream to createUIMessageStreamResponse so the stream is consumed even when aborted, preventing memory leaks or hanging connections. The onEnd callback's isAborted flag separates aborted from normal completion.
    
    ```typescript
    import { openai } from '@ai-sdk/openai';
    import {
      consumeStream,
      convertToModelMessages,
      createUIMessageStreamResponse,
      streamText,
      toUIMessageStream,
      UIMessage,
    } from 'ai';
    
    export async function POST(req: Request) {
      const { messages }: { messages: UIMessage[] } = await req.json();
    
      const result = streamText({
        model: "anthropic/claude-sonnet-5.5",
        messages: await convertToModelMessages(messages),
        abortSignal: req.signal,
      });
    
      return createUIMessageStreamResponse({
        stream: toUIMessageStream({
          stream: result.stream,
          onEnd: async ({ isAborted }) => {
            if (isAborted) {
              console.log('Stream was aborted');
              // Handle abort-specific cleanup
            } else {
              console.log('Stream completed normally');
              // Handle normal completion
            }
          },
        }),
        consumeSseStream: consumeStream,
      });
    }
    ```

    import { defineConfig } from 'oxlint';
    
    import baseConfig from '../../oxlint-base.config.mts';
    
    export default defineConfig({
      extends: [baseConfig],
      plugins: ['node'],
      env: {
        node: true,
      },
      rules: {
        'oxc/no-barrel-file': 'error',
      },
    });
    import { createOpenAICompatible } from '@ai-sdk/openai-compatible';
    import {
      aiDocumentFormats,
      injectDocumentStateMessages,
      toolDefinitionsToToolSet,
    } from '@blocknote/xl-ai/server';
    import { Inject, Injectable } from '@nestjs/common';
    import type { ConfigType } from '@nestjs/config';
    import {
      convertToModelMessages,
      stepCountIs,
      streamText,
      type UIMessage,
      type UIMessageChunk,
    } from 'ai';
    import { Traceable } from 'nestjs-otel';
    
    import { AuthorizationService } from '#/authorization/authorization.service';
    import { llmConfig } from '#/config.factory';
    import { NoteService } from '#/note/note.service';
    import { SearchService } from '#/search/search.service';
    
    import { createCustomTools } from './tools/custom-tools';
    
    export type BlockNoteChatRequest = {
      messages: UIMessage[];
      toolDefinitions?: Parameters<typeof toolDefinitionsToToolSet>[0];
    };
    
    @Injectable()
    @Traceable()
    export class AiService {
      constructor(
        @Inject(llmConfig.KEY) private readonly llm: ConfigType<typeof llmConfig>,
        private readonly noteClient: NoteService,
        private readonly search: SearchService,
        private readonly authorization: AuthorizationService
      ) {}
    
      async streamBlockNoteChat(
        body: BlockNoteChatRequest,
        userId: string
      ): Promise<ReadableStream<UIMessageChunk>> {
        const model = createOpenAICompatible({
          baseURL: this.llm.baseUrl,
          apiKey: this.llm.apiKey,
          name: 'llm',
        })(this.llm.model);
    
        const result = streamText({
          model,
          system: aiDocumentFormats.html.systemPrompt,
          messages: await convertToModelMessages(injectDocumentStateMessages(body.messages)),
          tools: {
            ...toolDefinitionsToToolSet(body.toolDefinitions ?? {}),
            ...createCustomTools({
              userId,
              noteClient: this.noteClient,
              search: this.search,
              authorization: this.authorization,
            }),
          },
          stopWhen: stepCountIs(10), // TODO: Parameterise this
        });
    
        return result.toUIMessageStream();
      }
    }

        import { ArgumentsHost, Catch, ExceptionFilter, HttpException, Logger } from '@nestjs/common';
        import type { Response } from 'express';
        import { status } from '@grpc/grpc-js';
        
        import { isGrpcError } from './grpc';
        
        export class AiError extends HttpException {
          constructor(statusCode: number, code: string, message: string, details?: Record<string, unknown>) {
            super({ code, message, ...details }, statusCode);
          }
        }
        
        export function publicError(error: unknown): { status: number; body: Record<string, unknown> } {
          if (error instanceof AiError) {
            return { status: error.getStatus(), body: error.getResponse() as Record<string, unknown> };
          }
          if (error instanceof HttpException) {
            return { status: error.getStatus(), body: { code: 'requestFailed', message: error.message } };
          }
          if (isGrpcError(error)) {
            if (error.code === status.PERMISSION_DENIED) {
              return { status: 403, body: { code: 'forbidden', message: 'Access denied.' } };
            }
            if (error.code === status.NOT_FOUND) {
              return { status: 404, body: { code: 'notFound', message: 'Resource not found.' } };
            }
            return { status: 503, body: { code: 'serviceUnavailable', message: 'A required service is unavailable.' } };
          }
          return { status: 500, body: { code: 'aiError', message: 'The AI request failed.' } };
        }
        
        @Catch()
        export class AiExceptionFilter implements ExceptionFilter {
          private readonly logger = new Logger(AiExceptionFilter.name);
        
          catch(error: unknown, host: ArgumentsHost) {
            const response = host.switchToHttp().getResponse<Response>();
            const mapped = publicError(error);
            if (mapped.status >= 500) this.logger.error({ err: error }, 'AI request failed');
            if (!response.headersSent) {
              if (mapped.status === 429) response.setHeader('Retry-After', '60');
              response.status(mapped.status).json(mapped.body);
            } else {
              response.end();
            }
          }
        }

        import { Inject, Injectable, Logger, OnModuleInit } from '@nestjs/common';
        import type { ClientGrpc } from '@nestjs/microservices';
        import {
          BILLING_PACKAGE_NAME, BILLING_SERVICE_NAME, type BillingServiceClient,
        } from '@notopia-uit/pb/billing';
        import { firstValueFrom, timeout } from 'rxjs';
        
        import { AiError } from '#/common/ai-error';
        
        @Injectable()
        export class BillingService implements OnModuleInit {
          private client!: BillingServiceClient;
          private readonly logger = new Logger(BillingService.name);
        
          constructor(@Inject(BILLING_PACKAGE_NAME) private readonly grpc: ClientGrpc) {}
        
          onModuleInit() {
            this.client = this.grpc.getService<BillingServiceClient>(BILLING_SERVICE_NAME);
          }
        
          async monthlyCredits(workspaceId: string): Promise<number> {
            try {
              const response = await firstValueFrom(
                this.client.getWorkspaceEntitlements({ workspaceId }).pipe(timeout(5000))
              );
              if (!response.entitlements || response.entitlements.workspaceId !== workspaceId) {
                throw new Error('Missing or mismatched billing entitlements');
              }
              const raw = response.entitlements.limits?.ai_credits_monthly;
              const credits = raw === undefined ? 0 : Number(raw);
              if (!Number.isSafeInteger(credits) || credits < -1) throw new Error('Invalid AI quota');
              return credits;
            } catch (error) {
              this.logger.error({ err: error }, 'Failed to fetch AI entitlements');
              throw new AiError(503, 'billingServiceUnavailable', 'Billing is unavailable. Please retry later.');
            }
          }
        }

        import { validateUIMessages, type UIMessage } from 'ai';
        import { z } from 'zod';
        
        import { AiError } from '#/common/ai-error';
        
        const jsonSchema = z.object({ type: z.literal('object') }).passthrough();
        const requestSchema = z.object({
          workspaceId: z.uuid().optional(),
          noteId: z.uuid().optional(),
          messages: z.array(z.object({
            id: z.string().min(1).max(200),
            role: z.enum(['user', 'assistant']),
            parts: z.array(z.unknown()).min(1).max(200),
          }).passthrough()).min(1).max(100),
          toolDefinitions: z.record(z.enum(['applyDocumentOperations']), z.object({
            description: z.string().max(10000).optional(),
            inputSchema: jsonSchema,
            outputSchema: z.record(z.string(), z.unknown()).optional(),
          })).optional(),
        });
        
        export type BlockNoteChatBody = Omit<z.infer<typeof requestSchema>, 'messages'> & { messages: UIMessage[] };
        
        export async function parseChatRequest(input: unknown): Promise<BlockNoteChatBody> {
          try {
            if (Buffer.byteLength(JSON.stringify(input) ?? '') > 512000) {
              throw new AiError(413, 'requestTooLarge', 'AI requests must be at most 500 KB.');
            }
            const body = requestSchema.parse(input);
            const messages = await validateUIMessages({ messages: body.messages });
            const last = messages.at(-1);
            if (last?.role !== 'user' || !last.parts.some(part => part.type === 'text' && part.text.trim())) {
              throw new Error('The final message must be a user prompt');
            }
            return { ...body, messages };
          } catch (error) {
            if (error instanceof AiError) throw error;
            throw new AiError(400, 'invalidAiRequest', 'Invalid messages, context, or tool definitions. End with a user prompt.');
          }
        }
