    import type { MyEditor } from '@blocknote/core';
    import { AIExtension } from '@blocknote/xl-ai';
    import { useCallback, useSyncExternalStore } from 'react';
    
    import { Alert, AlertDescription, AlertTitle } from './shadcn/alert';
    import { Button } from './shadcn/button';
    
    export function EditorAiError({ editor }: { editor: MyEditor }) {
      const ai = editor.getExtension(AIExtension);
      const subscribe = useCallback((listener: () => void) => ai?.store.subscribe(listener) ?? (() => {}), [ai]);
      const getSnapshot = useCallback(() => ai?.store.state.aiMenuState ?? 'closed', [ai]);
      const state = useSyncExternalStore(subscribe, getSnapshot, () => 'closed' as const);
      if (state === 'closed' || state.status !== 'error') return null;
      const message =
        state.error instanceof Error ? state.error.message : 'The AI request failed. Please try again.';
      return (
        <Alert variant="destructive" className="my-2">
          <AlertTitle>AI request failed</AlertTitle>
          <AlertDescription>{message}</AlertDescription>
          <Button
            type="button"
            variant="outline"
            size="sm"
            className="mt-2 w-fit"
            onClick={() => ai?.closeAIMenu()}
          >
            Dismiss
          </Button>
        </Alert>
      );
    }

    ### Implementing subscribe for window online and offline events
    
    Source: https://github.com/reactjs/react.dev/blob/main/src/content/reference/react/useSyncExternalStore.md
    
    Registers event listeners on window for online and offline events, returning a cleanup function to remove them.
    
    ```js
    function subscribe(callback) {
      window.addEventListener('online', callback);
      window.addEventListener('offline', callback);
      return () => {
        window.removeEventListener('online', callback);
        window.removeEventListener('offline', callback);
      };
    }
    ```
    
    --------------------------------
    
    ### Pass getServerSnapshot to useSyncExternalStore for server rendering
    
    Source: https://github.com/reactjs/react.dev/blob/main/src/content/reference/react/useSyncExternalStore.md
    
    Pass a getServerSnapshot function as the third argument to useSyncExternalStore to provide an initial snapshot during server rendering and hydration. Ensure getServerSnapshot returns the exact same data on the initial client render as it returned on the server.
    
    ```js
    import { useSyncExternalStore } from 'react';
    
    export function useOnlineStatus() {
      const isOnline = useSyncExternalStore(subscribe, getSnapshot, getServerSnapshot);
      return isOnline;
    }
    
    function getSnapshot() {
      return navigator.onLine;
    }
    
    function getServerSnapshot() {
      return true; // Always show "Online" for server-generated HTML
    }
    
    function subscribe(callback) {
      // ...
    }
    ```
    
    --------------------------------
    
    ### useSyncExternalStore(subscribe, getSnapshot)
    
    Source: https://github.com/reactjs/react.dev/blob/main/src/content/reference/react/useSyncExternalStore.md
    
    Subscribes to an external store or browser API and reads a snapshot of its value. Triggers a re-render whenever the store notifies React of changes via the subscribe callback.
    
    ```APIDOC
    ## useSyncExternalStore(subscribe, getSnapshot)
    
    ### Description
    A React Hook that lets you subscribe to an external store or browser API value that changes over time.
    
    ### Signature
    ```js
    const snapshot = useSyncExternalStore(subscribe, getSnapshot);
    ```
    
    ### Parameters
    - **subscribe** (`(callback: () => void) => () => void`) - Required. A function that takes a single `callback` argument and subscribes it to the store. It should return a cleanup function that removes the subscription.
    - **getSnapshot** (`() => any`) - Required. A function that reads and returns the current snapshot of the data from the external store/API.
    
    ### Return Value
    - **snapshot** (`any`) - The current snapshot of the external store returned by `getSnapshot`.
    
    ### Usage Example
    ```js
    import { useSyncExternalStore } from 'react';
    
    function getSnapshot() {
      return navigator.onLine;
    }
    
    function subscribe(callback) {
      window.addEventListener('online', callback);
      window.addEventListener('offline', callback);
      return () => {
        window.removeEventListener('online', callback);
        window.removeEventListener('offline', callback);
      };
    }
    
    export function useOnlineStatus() {
      return useSyncExternalStore(subscribe, getSnapshot);
    }
    ```
    ```
    
    --------------------------------
    
    ### useSyncExternalStore > Reference > useSyncExternalStore(subscribe, getSnapshot, getServerSnapshot?) > Caveats
    
    Source: https://github.com/reactjs/react.dev/blob/main/src/content/reference/react/useSyncExternalStore.md
    
    * The store snapshot returned by `getSnapshot` must be immutable. If the underlying store has mutable data, return a new immutable snapshot if the data has changed. Otherwise, return a cached last snapshot.
    
    * If a different `subscribe` function is passed during a re-render, React will re-subscribe to the store using the newly passed `subscribe` function. You can prevent this by declaring `subscribe` outside the component.
    
    * If the store is mutated during a [non-blocking Transition update](/reference/react/useTransition), React will fall back to performing that update as blocking. Specifically, for every Transition update, React will call `getSnapshot` a second time just before applying changes to the DOM. If it returns a different value than when it was called originally, React will restart the update from scratch, this time applying it as a blocking update, to ensure that every component on screen is reflecting the same version of the store.
    
    * It's not recommended to _suspend_ a render based on a store value returned by `useSyncExternalStore`. The reason is that mutations to the external store cannot be marked as [non-blocking Transition updates](/reference/react/useTransition), so they will trigger the nearest [`Suspense` fallback](/reference/react/Suspense), replacing already-rendered content on screen with a loading spinner, which typically makes a poor UX.
    
      For example, the following are discouraged:
    
    --------------------------------
    
    ### Return immutable data directly from getSnapshot
    
    Source: https://github.com/reactjs/react.dev/blob/main/src/content/reference/react/useSyncExternalStore.md
    
    Returns immutable store data directly from getSnapshot so that the snapshot identity only changes when the store data actually updates.
    
    ```javascript
    function getSnapshot() {
      // ✅ You can return immutable data
      return myStore.todos;
    }
    ```

    ### Infrastructure
    
    Layout:
    
    - `infrastructure/` — Authentik, Traefik, Redpanda, Meilisearch, RustFS, dbgate
    - `services/` — per-service dependencies (e.g. `note.yaml` = `note_postgresql` + `note_redis`)
    - `dev/`, `monitoring/`
    - `compose.yaml` — includes the above
    
    #### Authentik
    
    - Users/Client/Role list in `./deploy/compose/infrastructure/authentik-blueprints/users.yaml`
      > Read this file for login users. Must use Oauth2 flow, doesn't support direct access grant.
      > If you need debugging, use curl or anything related.
    - Frontend App in `./deploy/compose/infrastructure/authentik-blueprints/app-web.yaml`
      (includes JWKS, callback URL, etc.)
    - Blueprint docs at: <https://github.com/goauthentik/authentik/tree/main/website/docs/customize/blueprints>
    - When editing a blueprint, authentik will reconcile itself
    
    #### Traefik
    
    - Config in `./deploy/compose/infrastructure/traefik/`: static (`traefik.yaml`) and
      dynamic (`dynamic/*.yaml`, one file per service)
    - Dynamic config includes `agilezebra/jwt-middleware` for authentication; it authorizes
      using roles mapped from the OIDC `roles` claim, and injects user headers downstream
    - Traefik mounts the host network, so it can reach services at `localhost:{port}`
    - Backend services are routed by **path prefix on a single API host**, and each service
      excludes its own health path from the JWT middleware. For example:
      - `api.notopia.localhost/note`          -> note service (`/note/health` is unauthenticated)
      - `api.notopia.localhost/authorization` -> authorization service
      - `api.notopia.localhost/document`      -> document service
        (`/document/ws/document` is the Hocuspocus websocket route)
      - `api.notopia.localhost` (root)        -> api-web (Scalar spec viewer)
      - When adding a service, add `dynamic/{service}.yaml` and mirror this pattern.
        Any endpoint that must skip auth (e.g. a payment webhook) needs its own router
        without the JWT middleware.
    
    #### Local dev hosts
    
    All under `notopia.localhost`:
    
    | Host | What |
    | --- | --- |
    | `web.notopia.localhost` | Next.js web app |
    | `api.notopia.localhost` | All backend APIs, routed by path prefix (see above) |
    | `authentik.notopia.localhost` | Authentik (IdP) |
    | `traefik.notopia.localhost` | Traefik dashboard |
    | `rustfs-api.notopia.localhost` | RustFS S3 API endpoint |
    | `rustfs.notopia.localhost` | RustFS console |
    | `meilisearch.notopia.localhost` | Meilisearch |
    | `redpanda.notopia.localhost` | Redpanda console |
    | `dbgate.notopia.localhost` | dbgate (DB browser) |

    ### Run Ollama with CPU only
    
    Source: https://github.com/ollama/ollama/blob/main/docs/docker.mdx
    
    Starts an Ollama container using the CPU-only image. Mounts the ollama volume for model storage and exposes port 11434.
    
    ```shell
    docker run -d -v ollama:/root/.ollama -p 11434:11434 --name ollama ollama/ollama
    ```
    
    --------------------------------
    
    ### CPU only
    
    Source: https://github.com/ollama/ollama/blob/main/docs/docker.mdx
    
    ## CPU only
    
    ```shell
    docker run -d -v ollama:/root/.ollama -p 11434:11434 --name ollama ollama/ollama
    ```
    
    --------------------------------
    
    ### Pull Model Request (curl)
    
    Source: https://github.com/ollama/ollama/blob/main/docs/api.md
    
    Sends a POST request to /api/pull to download a model from the ollama library. The request body specifies the model name. Cancelled pulls resume from where they left off, and multiple calls share the same download progress.
    
    ```shell
    curl http://localhost:11434/api/pull -d '{
      "model": "llama3.2"
    }'
    ```
    
    --------------------------------
    
    ### Pull a model with ollama pull
    
    Source: https://github.com/ollama/ollama/blob/main/docs/integrations/nemoclaw.mdx
    
    Pulls the nemotron-3-nano:30b model from Ollama. This is the first step in the quick start.
    
    ```bash
    ollama pull nemotron-3-nano:30b
    ```
    
    --------------------------------
    
    ### CLI commands to list and pull models
    
    Source: https://github.com/ollama/ollama/blob/main/cmd/cmd.go

    ### Healthcheck config mapping and validation
    
    Source: https://github.com/docker/compose/blob/main/pkg/compose/convert.go
    
    Maps healthcheck fields (test, interval, timeout, start_period, start_interval, retries, disable) to Moby container config. Disable sets test to ["NONE"]. Validates that start_interval requires start_period to be set.
    
    ```go
    func (s *composeService) ToMobyHealthCheck(ctx context.Context, check *compose.HealthCheckConfig) (*container.HealthConfig, error) {
    	if check == nil {
    		return nil, nil
    	}
    	var (
    		interval time.Duration
    		timeout  time.Duration
    		period   time.Duration
    		retries  int
    	)
    	if check.Interval != nil {
    		interval = time.Duration(*check.Interval)
    	}
    	if check.Timeout != nil {
    		timeout = time.Duration(*check.Timeout)
    	}
    	if check.StartPeriod != nil {
    		period = time.Duration(*check.StartPeriod)
    	}
    	if check.Retries != nil {
    		retries = int(*check.Retries)
    	}
    	test := check.Test
    	if check.Disable {
    		test = []string{"NONE"}
    	}
    	var startInterval time.Duration
    	if check.StartInterval != nil {
    		startInterval = time.Duration(*check.StartInterval)
    		if check.StartPeriod == nil {
    			return nil, errors.New("healthcheck.start_interval requires healthcheck.start_period to be set")
    		}
    	}
    	return &container.HealthConfig{
    		Test:          test,
    		Interval:      interval,
    		Timeout:       timeout,
    		StartPeriod:   period,
    		StartInterval: startInterval,
    		Retries:       retries,
    	}, nil
    }
    ```

    ### depends_on with healthcheck and service_healthy condition
    
    Source: https://github.com/docker/compose/blob/main/pkg/e2e/testdata/TestRecreateWithNoDeps/compose.yaml
    
    Shows a service waiting on another with `depends_on: {dep: {condition: service_healthy}}` plus a matching `healthcheck`, the pattern requested for ordering against a healthy dependency rather than plain `docker run`.
    
    ```yaml
    services:
      my-service:
        image: alpine
        command: sleep infinity
        init: true
        depends_on:
          dep: {condition: service_healthy}
    
      dep:
        image: alpine
        command: sleep infinity
        init: true
        healthcheck:
          test:     "/bin/true"
          interval: 2s
          timeout:  1s
          retries:  10
    
    ```

    package billingfixtures
    
    import (
        "context"
        "errors"
        "log/slog"
        "time"
    
        "github.com/google/uuid"
        "github.com/notopia-uit/notopia/internal/billing/domain"
    )
    
    // Users come from deploy/compose/infrastructure/authentik-blueprints/users.yaml.
    // Provider ids are fake: Stripe actions on this workspace fail, entitlements work.
    var (
        workspaceID = uuid.MustParse("00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000110")
        payer       = domain.Payer{
            ID:    "110",
            Email: "user@notopia.com",
            Name:  "User",
        }
    )
    
    const (
        actor                  = "110"
        currency               = "vnd"
        fakeProviderCustomerID = "cus_fixture_110"
        fakeProviderPaymentID  = "pi_fixture_110"
    )
    
    type Fixtures struct {
        uow    domain.UnitOfWork
        logger *slog.Logger
    }
    
    func NewFixtures(uow domain.UnitOfWork, logger *slog.Logger) *Fixtures {
        return &Fixtures{
            uow:    uow,
            logger: logger,
        }
    }
    
    var ProvideFixtures = NewFixtures
    
    // Run is idempotent: skips when the workspace already has a subscription.
    func (f *Fixtures) Run(ctx context.Context) error {
        now := time.Now()
        return f.uow.Execute(ctx, func(r domain.RepoRegistry) error {
            existing, err := r.Subscription().GetCurrentByWorkspace(ctx, workspaceID, true)
            if err != nil {
                return err
            }
            if existing != nil {
                f.logger.InfoContext(ctx, "workspace already has a subscription, skipped", slog.String("workspaceId", workspaceID.String()))
                return nil
            }
            price, err := r.Price().GetActive(ctx, domain.PlanTierPro, domain.IntervalLifetime, currency, false)
            if err != nil {
                return err
            }
            if price == nil {
                return errors.New("pro lifetime price missing: run just seed-billing first")
            }
            account := domain.OpenBillingAccount(workspaceID, fakeProviderCustomerID, payer, now, actor)
            if err := r.BillingAccount().Save(ctx, account); err != nil {
                return err
            }
            sub, err := domain.NewLifetimeSubscription(uuid.Must(uuid.NewV7()), workspaceID, price, fakeProviderPaymentID, now, now, actor)
            if err != nil {
                return err
            }
            if err := r.Subscription().Save(ctx, sub); err != nil {
                return err
            }
            f.logger.InfoContext(ctx, "lifetime subscription created", slog.String("workspaceId", workspaceID.String()))
            return nil
        })
    }
    # Local AI testing
    
    The application services run on the host through Nx. Compose runs their infrastructure.
    The AI backend needs note and authorization gRPC, billing gRPC, Meilisearch, a model server,
    and its own Redis. Browser testing also needs web, Traefik and Authentik; document and
    search-worker provide live editor content and committed search results.
    
    From the repository root, start the normal infrastructure, including the new AI Redis:
    
    ```sh
    docker compose -f deploy/compose/compose.yaml up -d
    ```
    
    To start only the new Redis when the rest is already running:
    
    ```sh
    docker compose -f deploy/compose/compose.yaml up -d --wait ai_redis
    ```
    
    `apps/ai/.env` already uses `redis://127.0.0.1:6376`. Redis stores monthly credit counters
    and throttling state with AOF persistence and `noeviction`. A named volume preserves data
    across container recreation. `AI_REDIS_PORT` can override the published port; if changed,
    update `NOTOPIA_AI_REDIS_URL` in your local AI environment too.
    
    ## Optional local model server
    
    If Ollama is already running on the host at port 11434, skip this step. Otherwise:
    
    ```sh
    docker compose -f deploy/compose/compose.yaml --profile ai-local-llm up -d --wait ai_ollama
    docker compose -f deploy/compose/compose.yaml --profile ai-local-llm exec ai_ollama ollama pull qwen3:8b
    ```
    
    This matches the AI app's existing model and `http://localhost:11434/v1` base URL.
    The container uses CPU by default and stores downloaded models in a named volume. The
    model pull happens only when you run the second command. `AI_OLLAMA_IMAGE` can pin an image
    version; `AI_OLLAMA_PORT` can change the host port, with a matching AI base URL update.
    A different OpenAI-compatible model endpoint can be configured through the AI app's
    `NOTOPIA_AI_LLM_*` environment variables instead.
    
    ## Application and billing prerequisites
    
    Start note, authorization, billing, document, search-worker, web and AI using their normal
    Nx development targets. AI listens on 8085; its billing gRPC endpoint is localhost:18084.
    The health endpoint is `http://api.notopia.localhost/ai/health`.
    
    Use a workspace with AI credits: Free defaults to zero, while Plus/Pro provide credits.
    There is no need to make a real payment to test: the existing `just fixtures-billing`
    workflow creates a development Pro subscription with fake provider IDs for workspace
    `00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000110`. Follow the billing fixture prerequisites and use a
    user with membership in that workspace. Fake provider IDs support entitlement checks, not
    real Stripe checkout/refund actions.
    
    Open the workspace assistant, ask it to find/read notes, then test an editor AI command.
    Commit edited notes to make their latest content available to search and the assistant.
    Automatic commits may also do this when enabled by the workspace plan.
    
    AI currently charges one credit per started generation, including server tool steps, and
    resets usage on UTC calendar months. Provider errors and cancellation after start retain
    the credit. Missing Redis or billing causes a 503; a workspace without credits gets a 402.
    
    ## Automated Redis tests
    
    Use a separate test Redis rather than the Redis holding your manual-test credit counters.
    The integration tests take `AI_TEST_REDIS_URL` and use a random namespace:
    
    ```sh
    AI_TEST_REDIS_URL=redis://127.0.0.1:16385 nx test ai --skip-nx-cache
    ```
    
    Without that variable, the real-Redis cases are skipped; the remaining tests still run.
    NOTOPIA_AUTHORIZATIONFIXTURES_GENERAL_APP_ENV="development"
    
    NOTOPIA_AUTHORIZATIONFIXTURES_LOG_LEVEL=debug
    NOTOPIA_AUTHORIZATIONFIXTURES_LOG_PRETTY=true
    
    NOTOPIA_AUTHORIZATIONFIXTURES_DATABASE_URL=postgres://notopiauit:notopiauit@localhost:5439/authorization?sslmode=disable
    
    OTEL_SERVICE_NAME="authorizationfixtures"

Run this from the repository root. The application services run through Nx; Docker supplies their infrastructure.

**1. Start infrastructure**

```sh
docker compose -f deploy/compose/compose.yaml up -d
docker compose -f deploy/compose/compose.yaml up -d --wait ai_redis
```

If you don’t already have Ollama running:

```sh
docker compose -f deploy/compose/compose.yaml --profile ai-local-llm up -d --wait ai_ollama
docker compose -f deploy/compose/compose.yaml exec ai_ollama ollama pull qwen3:8b
```

**2. Prepare a workspace with credits**

Use your existing populated workspace with a Plus/Pro plan. Alternatively, the development billing fixture provides Pro for workspace `00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000110`:

```sh
just fixtures-billing
```

If it reports a missing Pro lifetime price, run `just seed-billing` first; that requires the existing Stripe sandbox configuration. The fixture also assumes your normal note and authorization fixtures are loaded.

The fixture login is `user` / `user`. Free workspaces should return **402**, so they cannot test successful generation.

**3. Start the applications**

In one terminal:

```sh
nx run-many -t run -p note,authorization,billing,document,search-worker,ai --parallel=6
```

In another:

```sh
nx dev web
```

Check:

```sh
curl -f http://api.notopia.localhost/ai/health
```

Then open `http://web.notopia.localhost` and sign in.

**4. Test the UI**

| Test | Action | Expected |
|---|---|---|
| Workspace assistant | Ask “Find notes about … and summarize one” | Search/read tool activity followed by a streamed answer |
| Attachments | Attach a note and ask for its summary | Assistant reads its committed content |
| Editor AI | Select text and invoke a BlockNote AI command | Suggested edits appear in that note |
| Commit | Edit a note, click **Commit changes**, then search for the new content | Content becomes available after indexing |
| Stop | Stop a running answer | Generation stops and another request can start |
| Note switching | Switch notes and invoke AI again | Request uses the new note’s ID |
| Error recovery | Stop billing temporarily and submit a request | Readable unavailable error; **Edit prompt** restores your input |

In browser DevTools → Network, inspect `POST /ai`: assistant requests should contain `workspaceId`; editor requests should contain `noteId`.

**5. Check enforcement**

- Submit from a Free workspace → **402** with readable credit/reset information.
- Replay an identical successful request with the same message ID → **409**, without another credit charge.
- Change the workspace ID to one the user cannot access → **403**.
- Exceed the concurrent-stream limit → **429**.

Started generations consume a credit, including ones you stop.

**6. Run automated regression tests**

Start an isolated test Redis:

```sh

AI_TEST_REDIS_URL=redis://127.0.0.1:16385 nx test ai --skip-nx-cache
nx test packages/ui

docker stop notopia-ai-test-redis
```

    # AI Service (nx: `ai`)
    
    NestJS HTTP backend for BlockNote AI and workspace assistant chat. No database or Kafka;
    uses note, authorization and billing gRPC, Meilisearch, and Redis for shared accounting.
    
    ## Modules
    
    | Module | Role |
    | --- | --- |
    | `ai/` | `POST /ai`, runtime validation, tool selection, AI SDK v6 UI-message stream |
    | `note/` | User-aware note metadata and workspace lookups over gRPC |
    | `authorization/` | Workspace discovery, read/write permission checks |
    | `billing/` | Uncached workspace entitlements and live upgrade plan lookup over gRPC |
    | `search/` | Workspace-filtered committed content search and bounded indexed content reads |
    | `usage/` | Redis Lua: per-user throttle/stream leases, workspace monthly credits, duplicate requests |
    | `common/` | Gateway user guard, normalized HTTP errors |
    
    ## Request flow and context
    
    Browser → Traefik JWT middleware → `POST /ai` → LLM → AI SDK SSE response.
    There is no web proxy. `GET /ai/health` remains unauthenticated.
    
    Requests contain `messages`, optional BlockNote `toolDefinitions`, and context supplied as
    `workspaceId`, `noteId`, or `X-Workspace-Id`. Conflicting contexts are rejected. `noteId`
    is resolved using a user-aware note RPC. Without explicit context, exactly one accessible
    workspace is required; zero or multiple workspaces return 400 `workspaceRequired`.
    The web assistant sends workspaceId and editors (including previews) send noteId through the shared UI transport; other clients need to send context; do not infer billing from prompt text,
    attached note labels, a model tool argument, or an untrusted Referer.
    
    HTTP trusts gateway-injected `x-forwarded-id`; the backend must not be exposed to untrusted
    traffic bypassing Traefik. User ID is the throttle key. Forwarded client IP is not used:
    a trusted proxy chain has not been configured for this service.
    
    ## Billing and accounting
    
    Billing owns subscriptions and resolves `ai_credits_monthly`. AI fetches it on every generation
    (no entitlement cache or subscription-event consumer). Missing quota means zero, `-1` means
    unlimited. Permission is checked before billing. Billing failure → 503
    `billingServiceUnavailable`; exhausted quota → 402 `planLimitExceeded` with the same
    `details` shape as note/document (`kind`, `key`, `current`, `max`, `requiredPlan`) and `resetAt`.
    Upgrade options come from billing's `ListPlans`, not hardcoded quota values.
    
    Policy: one credit per accepted generation, including server tool steps. Usage resets at
    00:00 UTC on the first of each calendar month, not the payment-provider renewal date (the
    current gRPC contract has no billing-period fields). A reserved credit is refunded only on
    confirmed failure/cancellation before generation starts. Once started, provider errors,
    timeouts and client disconnects retain the charge, because provider work may have occurred.
    A crash or uncertain Redis write is conservatively not refunded automatically.
    
    Last user message IDs deduplicate requests per user/workspace/month. A duplicate returns 409
    without another debit or replaying a response. Retry/regenerate with a new user message ID.
    Requests must end with a user prompt; client tool-result-only continuation is not supported.
    BlockNote's streamed editor tools and server tool loops are supported within a generation.
    
    `NOTOPIA_AI_REDIS_URL` must point to a dedicated, persistent, **noeviction** Redis 6.2+.
    There is no in-memory fallback for quota accounting; missing/down Redis returns 503
    `aiUsageUnavailable`. The Lua scripts use multiple keys and require standalone Redis (not
    Redis Cluster). Counters/deduplication survive until seven days after the month resets;
    active stream leases expire after the bounded request timeout plus a grace period.
    Redis loss can lose usage history: persistence/backups are an operational requirement.
    
    ## Tools and errors
    
    Read `HOW_TO_ADD_TOOLS.md` before adding tools. All server tools recheck workspace read access
    at execution. Search is filtered by validated workspace ID and results pass live note
    permission/trash/workspace checks. Indexed content may be stale and is never advertised as
    live document content. No tool calls another service's public REST API.
    
    Only BlockNote `applyDocumentOperations` client definitions are accepted, and require write
    permission at admission. Execution is client-side, with document authorization enforced by
    Hocuspocus. General chat includes workspace discovery; editor requests omit that tool.
    Do not set `toolChoice: 'none'` or force a tool call.
    
    Before response headers, errors are JSON `{ code, message, ... }` with 400/401/402/403/409/
    413/429/503/504 as appropriate. 429 includes `Retry-After`. After headers, provider errors use
    AI SDK stream error parts with a safe message; server tool failures are sanitized before
    AI SDK serializes them. The shared UI transport normalizes HTTP JSON into readable errors for workspace chat and BlockNote. Remote file parts are rejected to avoid server-side URL fetches.
    
    ## Configuration and checks
    
    `NOTOPIA_AI_SERVICES_BILLING_GRPC_URL` joins existing note/authorization endpoints.
    Defaults: `NOTOPIA_AI_REQUESTS_PER_MINUTE=20`, `NOTOPIA_AI_CONCURRENT_STREAMS=2`,
    `NOTOPIA_AI_TIMEOUT_MS=120000`, `NOTOPIA_AI_MAX_OUTPUT_TOKENS=4096` (per model step),
    `NOTOPIA_AI_MAX_STEPS=10`. The timeout covers setup and generation. Model credentials remain
    `NOTOPIA_AI_LLM_{BASE_URL,API_KEY,MODEL}`.

    # UI Package (`packages/ui`)
    
    Shared React components and utilities for `@notopia-uit/ui`. Uses shadcn/ui + Tailwind CSS.
    
    ## Error Handling
    
    ### Components
    
    | File | Export | Purpose |
    |---|---|---|
    | `components/error-boundary.tsx` | `ErrorBoundary` | Class-based React error boundary with retry. Props: `fallbackTitle`, `fallback` (render prop) Default UI shows error badge + retry button. |
    | `components/not-found.tsx` | `NotFound` | Reusable 404 page. Props: `resource` (optional, e.g. "Note", "Workspace"). Shows 404 badge, title, message, and "Go Home" link. |
    | `components/error-alert.tsx` | `ErrorAlert` | Static destructive alert box for inline error display. |
    | `components/error-button.tsx` | `ErrorButton` | 404 page with "Go Back Home" link button. |
    | `hooks/query-error-fallback.tsx` | `QueryErrorFallback` | React Query error fallback with retry. Used in 6+ client components. |
    
    ### Utilities
    
    | File | Export | Purpose |
    |---|---|---|
    | `lib/errors.ts` | `AppError` | Base error class extending `Error`. Properties: `code`, `moreInfo`, `statusCode`. |
    | `lib/errors.ts` | `NoteServiceError` | Note service API error subclass. |
    | `lib/errors.ts` | `DocumentServiceError` | Document service API error subclass. |
    | `lib/errors.ts` | `UnauthorizedError` | 401 unauthorized error subclass. |
    | `lib/errors.ts` | `NotFoundError` | 404 not found error subclass. |
    | `lib/errors.ts` | `toAppError(err)` | Normalizes any caught value into typed `AppError`. |
    | `lib/errors.ts` | `is404(err)` | Guard to detect 404 errors. |
    | `lib/errors.ts` | `GeneratedError` | Interface matching codegen error shapes (`{ code, message, more_info? }`). |
    
    ### Architecture
    
    ```
    Caught value (unknown)
        │
        ▼
    toAppError(err)  ──→  AppError (typed)
        │                      │
        │              ┌───────┴───────┐
        │              │               │
        ▼              ▼               ▼
    is404()       statusCode       code
    check         switch           match
    ```
    
    ### Adding New Error Subclasses
    
    1. Add the class to `lib/errors.ts` extending `AppError`
    2. Update `toAppError()` to detect and instantiate it (match on status code or error shape)
    3. Export from `lib/errors.ts` (already re-exported via `src/index.ts`)
    
    ### Pattern: Client Component Boundary Wrappers
    
    Since Next.js App Router pages are server components, use this pattern to add error boundaries around client components:
    
    ```tsx
    // my-component-boundary.tsx
    'use client';
    
    import { ErrorBoundary } from '@notopia-uit/ui/components/error-boundary';
    import MyComponent from '@notopia-uit/ui/components/my-component';
    
    export function MyComponentBoundary(props: Props) {
      return (
        <ErrorBoundary fallbackTitle="Component Error">
          <MyComponent {...props} />
        </ErrorBoundary>
      );
    }
    ```
    
    Then import the boundary wrapper in the server component page instead of the component directly.
    
    ### Avoid access process.env here
    
    We will pass the from the consumer packages like `apps/web` as props. This is guarded by oxlint

    import { Chat } from "@ai-sdk/react";
    import { UIMessage } from "ai";
    import merge from "lodash.merge";
    import {
      setupToolCallStreaming,
      streamToolsToToolSet,
      toolSetToToolDefinitions,
    } from "../../streamTool/index.js";
    import { AIRequest } from "./types.js";
    
    /**
     * Submits a message to the LLM, similar to `chat.sendMessage`, but in addition:
     * - adds the document state to the message metadata
     * - sets up tool call streaming (so that BlockNote tool calls will be applied to the editor)
     *
     * (should not throw any errors)
     *
     * @param chat - the AI SDK Chat instance
     * @param aiRequest - the AI request (create using {@link buildAIRequest})
     * @param message - the message to send to the LLM (optional, defaults to the last message)
     * @param options - the `ChatRequestOptions` to pass to the `chat.sendMessage` method (custom metadata, body, etc)
     * @param abortSignal - Optional AbortSignal to cancel ongoing tool call operations
     *
     * @returns the result of the tool call processing. Consumer should check both `chat.status` and `result.ok`;
     * - `chat.status` indicates if the LLM request succeeeded
     * - `result` will indicate if the BlockNote tool calls were processed successfully
     */
    export async function sendMessageWithAIRequest(
      chat: Chat<UIMessage>,
      aiRequest: AIRequest,
      message?: Parameters<Chat<UIMessage>["sendMessage"]>[0],
      options?: Parameters<Chat<UIMessage>["sendMessage"]>[1],
      abortSignal?: AbortSignal,
    ) {
      const sendingMessage = message ?? chat.lastMessage;
    
      if (!sendingMessage) {
        throw new Error("No message to send");
      }
    
      sendingMessage.metadata = merge(sendingMessage.metadata, {
        documentState: aiRequest.documentState,
      });
    
      const toolCallProcessing = setupToolCallStreaming(
        aiRequest.streamTools,
        chat,
        aiRequest.onStart,
        abortSignal,
      );
      options = merge(options, {
        metadata: {
          source: "blocknote-ai",
        },
        body: {
          toolDefinitions: await toolSetToToolDefinitions(
            streamToolsToToolSet(aiRequest.streamTools),
          ),
        },
      });
    
      await chat.sendMessage(message, options);
    
      const result = await toolCallProcessing;
      return result;
    }
      };
    }
    
    export function streamToolsToToolSet(streamTools: StreamTool<any>[]): ToolSet {
      return {
        applyDocumentOperations: {
          inputSchema: jsonSchema(createStreamToolsArraySchema(streamTools)),
          outputSchema: jsonSchema({ type: "object" }),
        },
      };
    }

    ### AIExtension usage with useCreateBlockNote
    
    Source: https://github.com/typecellos/blocknote/blob/main/docs/content/docs/features/ai/reference.mdx
    
    Use AIExtension to create a new AI extension and register it in the editor's extensions array when calling useCreateBlockNote. The options object includes agentCursor, transport, chatProvider, streamToolsProvider, chatRequestOptions, and documentStateBuilder.
    
    ```typescript
    // Usage:
    useCreateBlockNote({
      // Register the AI extension
      extensions: [AIExtension(options)],
      // other editor options
    });
    
    type AIExtensionOptions = AIRequestHelpers & {
      /**
       * The name and color of the agent cursor when the AI is writing
       * @default { name: "AI", color: "#8bc6ff" }
       */
      agentCursor?: { name: string; color: string };
    };
    
    type AIRequestHelpers = {
      /**
       * Transport used by the AI SDK to send requests to your backend/LLM.
       * Implement to customize backend URLs or use a different transport (e.g. websockets).
       */
      transport?: ChatTransport<UIMessage>;
    
      /**
       * Use the ChatProvider to customize how the AI SDK Chat instance is created.
       * For example, when you want to reuse an existing Chat instance used in the rest of your application.
       *
       * @note you cannot use both `chatProvider` and `transport` together.
       */
      chatProvider?: () => Chat<UIMessage>;
    
      /**
       * Customize which stream tools are available to the LLM.
       */
      streamToolsProvider?: StreamToolsProvider<any, any>;
      // Provide `streamToolsProvider` in AIExtension(options) or override per call via InvokeAIOptions.
      // If omitted, defaults to using `aiDocumentFormats.html.getStreamToolsProvider()`.
    
      /**
       * Extra options (headers/body/metadata) forwarded to the AI SDK request.
       */
      chatRequestOptions?: ChatRequestOptions;
    
      /**
       * Build the serializable document state that will be forwarded to the backend.
       *
       * @default aiDocumentFormats.html.defaultDocumentStateBuilder
       */
      documentStateBuilder?: DocumentStateBuilder<any>;
    };
    
    ```
    
    --------------------------------
    
    ### Create editor with AIExtension
    
    Source: https://github.com/typecellos/blocknote/blob/main/docs/content/docs/features/ai/getting-started.mdx
    
    Creates a BlockNote editor with the AI extension enabled, using DefaultChatTransport to connect to an API endpoint. Includes translations and the AI stylesheet.
    
    ```ts
    import { createBlockNoteEditor } from "@blocknote/core";
    import { BlockNoteAIExtension } from "@blocknote/xl-ai";
    import { en } from "@blocknote/core/locales";
    import { en as aiEn } from "@blocknote/xl-ai/locales";
    import { AIExtension } from "@blocknote/xl-ai";
    import "@blocknote/xl-ai/style.css"; // add the AI stylesheet
    
    const editor = createBlockNoteEditor({
      dictionary: {
        ...en,
        ai: aiEn, // add default translations for the AI extension
      },
      extensions: [
        AIExtension({
          transport: new DefaultChatTransport({
            api: `/api/chat`,
          }),
        }),
      ],
      // ... other editor options
    });
    ```
    
    --------------------------------
    
    ### AIExtensionInstance type definition
    
    Source: https://github.com/typecellos/blocknote/blob/main/docs/content/docs/features/ai/reference.mdx
    
    Defines the shape of the AIExtension instance returned by editor.getExtension(AIExtension). Includes methods for invoking AI, managing the AI menu, accepting/rejecting changes, retrying, aborting, and updating the AI response status. The store property holds the AI menu state, and options holds the global configuration.
    
    ```typescript
    type AIExtensionInstance = {
      /**
       * Execute a call to an LLM and apply the result to the editor
       */
      invokeAI(opts: InvokeAIOptions): Promise<void>;
    
      /**
       * Returns a read-only Tanstack Store with the state of the AI Menu
       */
      get store(): Store<{
        aiMenuState:
          | ({
              /**
               * The ID of the block that the AI menu is opened at.
               * This changes as the AI is making changes to the document
               */
              blockId: string;
            } & (
              | {
                  status: "error";
                  error: any;
                }
              | {
                  status:
                    | "user-input"
                    | "thinking"
                    | "ai-writing"
                    | "user-reviewing";
                }
            ))
          | "closed";
      }>;
    
      /**
       * Returns a Tanstack Store with the global configuration of the AI Extension.
       * These options are used by default across all LLM calls when calling {@link invokeAI}
       */
      readonly options: Store<AIRequestHelpers>;
    
      /** Open the AI menu at a specific block */
      openAIMenuAtBlock(blockID: string): void;
      /** Close the AI menu */
      closeAIMenu(): void;
      /** Accept the changes made by the LLM */
      acceptChanges(): void;
      /** Reject the changes made by the LLM */
      rejectChanges(): void;
      /** Retry the previous LLM call (only valid when status is "error") */
      retry(): Promise<void>;
      /** Abort the current LLM request */
      abort(reason?: any): Promise<void>;
      /** Advanced: manually update the status shown by the AI menu */
      setAIResponseStatus(
        status:
          | "user-input"
          | "thinking"
          | "ai-writing"
          | "user-reviewing"
          | { status: "error"; error: any },
      ): void;
    };
    ```

    ### buildAIRequest function signature
    
    Source: https://github.com/typecellos/blocknote/blob/main/docs/content/docs/features/ai/reference.mdx
    
    Use to assemble an AIRequest from editor state when bypassing invokeAI and calling sendMessageWithAIRequest directly.
    
    ```typescript
    async function buildAIRequest(opts: {
      editor: BlockNoteEditor;
      useSelection?: boolean;
      deleteEmptyCursorBlock?: boolean;
      streamToolsProvider?: StreamToolsProvider<any, any>;
      documentStateBuilder?: DocumentStateBuilder<any>;
      onBlockUpdated?: (blockId: string) => void;
      onStart?: () => void;
    }): Promise<AIRequest>;
    ```

    ### InvokeAIOptions type definition
    
    Source: https://github.com/typecellos/blocknote/blob/main/docs/content/docs/features/ai/reference.mdx
    
    Defines the options object passed to invokeAI. Includes the user prompt, whether to use the editor selection (default true), whether to delete an empty cursor block (default true), and allows overriding AIRequestHelpers per call.
    
    ```typescript
    type InvokeAIOptions = {
      /** The user prompt */
      userPrompt: string;
    
      /** Whether to use the editor selection for the LLM call (default: true) */
      useSelection?: boolean;
    
      /**
       * If the user's cursor is in an empty paragraph, automatically delete it when the AI starts writing.
       * Used when typing `/ai` in an empty block. (default: true)
       */
      deleteEmptyCursorBlock?: boolean;
    } & AIRequestHelpers; // Optionally override helpers per request
    ```

## Assistant

**I reused it inside the note editor. I did not connect it to the separate workspace assistant.** My earlier description made that distinction unclear.

“Editor session” means **a running editor connected to one particular note**. It includes:

- That note’s current content and block IDs.
- Your selected text and cursor position.
- Its live connection for syncing changes.
- The AI editing machinery that applies and reviews changes.

For example, when you open **“Meeting notes”**, the browser creates an editor for that note. If you select a paragraph and ask “Make this shorter,” BlockNote already knows exactly which paragraph to change.

The existing path is:

```text
You invoke AI inside the note editor
    ↓
BlockNote sends current document state + applyDocumentOperations definition
    ↓
AI service gives that tool definition to the model
    ↓
Model returns editing operations
    ↓
BlockNote applies them to that editor for review
```

You can see the two connection points:

- [editor-core.tsx:151](/home/ntgnguyen/Projects/notopia/packages/ui/src/components/editor-core.tsx:151) creates the collaborative editor and installs `AIExtension({ transport })`.
- [ai.service.ts:86](/home/ntgnguyen/Projects/notopia/apps/ai/src/ai/ai.service.ts:86) receives BlockNote’s tool definitions and merges them with our server tools.

**The definition describes what the model can request. The actual code that edits the document runs inside BlockNote in the browser.** Adding its name to the backend does not provide that executor.

Now consider asking the workspace assistant:

> “Open Meeting notes and shorten its introduction.”

The assistant currently has a chat and workspace ID, but no running editor for “Meeting notes.” Attaching the note only sends its ID and name—it does not create an editor.

To support that request, we still need to:

1. Load that note into an editor connected to its live document.
2. Send its current blocks and editing tool definition to the model.
3. Route the returned operations to that specific editor.
4. Let you review the changes and handle switching notes, cancellation, and cleanup.

**A sidebar beside an already-open editor is the easiest first version:** we can connect the assistant to that existing editor. Editing arbitrary unopened notes requires managing those additional editor sessions.

BlockNote provides helpers for sharing chat and building requests from editor state, so this is achievable. I left that integration unfinished; it is not a fundamental limitation. [BlockNote AI reference](https://github.com/typecellos/blocknote/blob/main/docs/content/docs/features/ai/reference.mdx)

    @Injectable()

        @Inject(usageConfig.KEY) private readonly config: ConfigType<typeof usageConfig>,

      async resolveWorkspace(body: BlockNoteChatBody, userId: string, headerWorkspace?: string) {
        if (headerWorkspace && !z.uuid().safeParse(headerWorkspace).success) {
          throw new AiError(400, 'invalidWorkspace', 'X-Workspace-Id must be a UUID.');
        }
        if (body.workspaceId && headerWorkspace && body.workspaceId !== headerWorkspace) {
          throw new AiError(400, 'invalidWorkspace', 'Workspace contexts do not match.');
        }
        let workspaceId = body.workspaceId ?? headerWorkspace;
        if (body.noteId) {
          const workspace = await this.noteClient.getNoteWorkspace(userId, body.noteId);
          if (!workspace || (workspaceId && workspaceId !== workspace.id)) {
            throw new AiError(403, 'forbidden', 'Note is outside this workspace.');
          }
          workspaceId = workspace.id;
        }
        if (!workspaceId) {
          const workspaces = await this.authorization.getUserWorkspaces({ userId });
          if (workspaces.length !== 1) {
            throw new AiError(
              400,
              'workspaceRequired',
              'Provide workspaceId, noteId, or X-Workspace-Id for AI billing and tools.'
            );
          }
          workspaceId = workspaces[0].workspaceId;
        }
        const permissions = await this.authorization.permissions(userId, workspaceId);
        if (!permissions.canRead) throw new AiError(403, 'forbidden', 'Workspace access denied.');
        if (Object.keys(body.toolDefinitions ?? {}).length && !permissions.canWrite) {
          throw new AiError(403, 'forbidden', 'Editing tools require workspace write permission.');
        }
        return workspaceId;
      }
    
      async streamBlockNoteChat(
        body: BlockNoteChatBody,
        userId: string,
        signal: AbortSignal,
        headerWorkspace?: string
      ): Promise<ReadableStream<UIMessageChunk>> {
        await this.usage.throttle(userId);

        resetAt: resetAt.toISOString(),

    }

        try {
          if (!this.redis) throw new Error('NOTOPIA_AI_REDIS_URL is not configured');
          return await this.redis.eval(script, keys.length, ...keys, ...args);
        } catch (error) {
          this.logger.error({ err: error }, 'AI usage accounting unavailable');
          throw new AiError(
            503,
            'aiUsageUnavailable',
            'AI usage accounting is unavailable. Please retry later.'
          );
        }
      }
    
      async throttle(userId: string) {
        const user = createHash('sha256').update(userId).digest('hex');
        const accepted = await this.eval(
          THROTTLE,
          [`ai:attempts:${user}`],
          [this.config.requestsPerMinute]
        );
        if (accepted !== 1)
          throw new AiError(429, 'aiRateLimited', 'Too many AI requests. Please retry later.');
      }
    
      async reserve(workspaceId: string, userId: string, messageId: string, credits: number) {
        const period = usagePeriod();
        if (credits === 0) {
          throw new AiError(402, 'aiCreditsExhausted', 'This workspace has no AI credits available.', {
            limit: credits,
            resetAt: period.resetAt,
          });
        }
        const digest = (value: string) => createHash('sha256').update(value).digest('hex');
        const user = digest(userId);
        const id = randomUUID();
        const keys = [
          `ai:usage:${workspaceId}:${period.month}`,
          `ai:request:${workspaceId}:${period.month}:${digest(JSON.stringify([userId, messageId]))}`,
          `ai:streams:${user}`,
          `ai:rate:${user}`,
        ];
        const result = await this.eval(RESERVE, keys, [
          Date.now(),
          credits,
          period.expiresAt,
          this.config.concurrentStreams,
          this.config.requestsPerMinute,
          this.config.timeoutMs + 5000,
          id,
        ]);
        if (result === 'duplicate')
          throw new AiError(
            409,
            'duplicateAiRequest',
            'This prompt has already been submitted. Send a new message to generate again.'
          );
        if (result === 'rate' || result === 'concurrency')
          throw new AiError(429, 'aiRateLimited', 'Too many AI requests. Please retry later.');
        if (result === 'quota')
          throw new AiError(402, 'aiCreditsExhausted', 'Monthly AI credits are exhausted.', {
            limit: credits,
            resetAt: period.resetAt,
          });
        if (result !== 'ok')
          throw new AiError(503, 'aiUsageUnavailable', 'Could not reserve AI credits.');
        let released = false;
        return {
          start: async () => {
            const started = await this.eval(START, [keys[1]], [id]);
            if (started !== 1)
              throw new AiError(409, 'duplicateAiRequest', 'This generation cannot be started again.');
          },
          release: async (refund = false) => {
            if (released) return;
            await this.eval(RELEASE, keys.slice(0, 3), [id, refund ? '1' : '0']);
            released = true;
          },
        };
      }
    }

    import { AiError } from '#/common/ai-error';
    
    const jsonSchema = z.object({ type: z.literal('object') }).passthrough();
    const requestSchema = z.object({
      workspaceId: z.uuid().optional(),
      noteId: z.uuid().optional(),
      messages: z
        .array(
          z
            .object({
              id: z.string().min(1).max(200),
              role: z.enum(['user', 'assistant']),
              parts: z.array(z.unknown()).min(1).max(200),

        )
        .min(1)

      toolDefinitions: z
        .partialRecord(

          z.object({
            description: z.string().max(10000).optional(),
            inputSchema: jsonSchema,

          })

    export type BlockNoteChatBody = Omit<z.infer<typeof requestSchema>, 'messages'> & {
      messages: UIMessage[];
    };
    
    export async function parseChatRequest(input: unknown): Promise<BlockNoteChatBody> {
      try {
        if (Buffer.byteLength(JSON.stringify(input) ?? '') > 512000) {
          throw new AiError(413, 'requestTooLarge', 'AI requests must be at most 500 KB.');
        }
        const body = requestSchema.parse(input);
        const messages = await validateUIMessages({ messages: body.messages });
        if (messages.some((message) => message.parts.some((part) => part.type === 'file'))) {
          throw new Error('Remote file attachments are not supported');
        }
        const last = messages.at(-1);
        if (
          last?.role !== 'user' ||
          !last.parts.some((part) => part.type === 'text' && part.text.trim())
        ) {
          throw new Error('The final message must be a user prompt');
        }
        return { ...body, messages };
      } catch (error) {
        if (error instanceof AiError) throw error;
        throw new AiError(
          400,
          'invalidAiRequest',
          'Invalid messages, context, or tool definitions. End with a user prompt.'
        );
      }
    }

    export class AiRequestError extends AppError {

    export async function fetchAi(input: RequestInfo | URL, init?: RequestInit): Promise<Response> {
      const response = await fetch(input, init);
      if (response.ok) return response;
      const body = await response.json().catch(() => null);
      const code = typeof body?.code === 'string' ? body.code : 'aiRequestFailed';
      let message = 'The AI request failed. Please try again.';
      if (response.status === 401) message = 'Your session expired. Sign in again to use AI.';
      else if (response.status === 402) {
        message = 'This workspace has no AI credits available.';
        if (typeof body?.resetAt === 'string' && !Number.isNaN(Date.parse(body.resetAt))) {
          message += ` Credits reset on ${new Date(body.resetAt).toLocaleDateString(undefined, { timeZone: 'UTC', dateStyle: 'medium' })} (UTC).`;
        }
      } else if (response.status === 403)
        message = 'You do not have permission to use AI for this note or workspace.';
      else if (response.status === 429)
        message = 'Too many AI requests. Wait a minute, then try again.';
      else if (response.status === 503)
        message = 'AI is temporarily unavailable. Please try again later.';
      else if (response.status === 504) message = 'The AI request timed out. Try a shorter prompt.';
      else if (typeof body?.message === 'string') message = body.message;
      throw new AiRequestError(message, response.status, code);
    }

        headers: async () => ({ Authorization: `Bearer ${await fetchAccessTokenClientSide()}` }),
        fetch: fetchAi,
      });
    }

    export type NoteHit = {
      id: string;
      workspaceId: string;
      name: string;
      folderId?: string;
      folderName?: string;
      tags?: string[];
      excerpt: string;
    };
    
    @Injectable()
    export class SearchService {
      private readonly meili: Meilisearch;
    
      constructor(@Inject(servicesConfig.KEY) services: ConfigType<typeof servicesConfig>) {
        this.meili = new Meilisearch({
          host: services.meiliHost,
          apiKey: services.meiliApiKey,
          timeout: 5000,
        });
      }
    
      async searchNotes({
        query,
        workspaceId,
        limit = 5,
      }: {
        query: string;
        workspaceId: string;
        limit?: number;
      }): Promise<NoteHit[]> {
        z.uuid().parse(workspaceId);
        const result = await this.meili.index('notes').search(query, {
          filter: `workspaceId = "${workspaceId}"`,
          limit: Math.min(20, Math.max(1, limit)),
          attributesToRetrieve: [
            'id',
            'workspaceId',
            'name',
            'folderId',
            'folderName',
            'tags',
            'plainTextContent',
            'trashed',
          ],
        });
        return result.hits
          .filter(
            (hit) =>
              !hit.trashed && hit.workspaceId === workspaceId && z.uuid().safeParse(hit.id).success
          )
          .map((hit) => ({
            id: String(hit.id),
            workspaceId,
            name: String(hit.name ?? '').slice(0, 1000),
            folderId: hit.folderId as string | undefined,
            folderName: hit.folderName as string | undefined,
            tags: hit.tags as string[] | undefined,
            excerpt: String(hit.plainTextContent ?? '').slice(0, 1500),
          }));
      }
    
      async readIndexedNoteContent(noteId: string, workspaceId: string) {
        z.uuid().parse(noteId);
        z.uuid().parse(workspaceId);
        try {
          const document = await this.meili.index('notes').getDocument(noteId, {
            fields: ['id', 'workspaceId', 'name', 'plainTextContent', 'trashed'],
          });
          if (document.workspaceId !== workspaceId || document.trashed) return null;
          const content = String(document.plainTextContent ?? '');
          return {
            noteId,
            name: document.name,
            content: content.slice(0, 20000),
            truncated: content.length > 20000,
            source: 'committed-search-index',
            mayBeStale: true,
          };
        } catch (error) {
          if (error instanceof MeilisearchApiError && error.cause?.code === 'document_not_found')
            return null;
          throw new AiError(503, 'searchUnavailable', 'Indexed note content is unavailable.');
        }
      }
    }

            })
            .pipe(timeout(5000))
        );
        return result.hasPermission;

        this.logger.debug('Fetching user workspaces for tool call');
        const response = await firstValueFrom(

        );

          workspaceId: workspace.id,
          role: String(workspace.role),
        }));
      }

    import { status } from '@grpc/grpc-js';
    import { ArgumentsHost, Catch, ExceptionFilter, HttpException, Logger } from '@nestjs/common';
    import type { Response } from 'express';
    
    import { isGrpcError } from './grpc';
    
    export class AiError extends HttpException {
      constructor(
        statusCode: number,
        code: string,
        message: string,
        details?: Record<string, unknown>
      ) {
        super({ code, message, ...details }, statusCode);
      }
    }
    
    export function publicError(error: unknown): { status: number; body: Record<string, unknown> } {
      if (error instanceof AiError) {
        return { status: error.getStatus(), body: error.getResponse() as Record<string, unknown> };
      }
      if (error instanceof HttpException) {
        return { status: error.getStatus(), body: { code: 'requestFailed', message: error.message } };
      }
      if (isGrpcError(error)) {
        if (error.code === status.PERMISSION_DENIED) {
          return { status: 403, body: { code: 'forbidden', message: 'Access denied.' } };
        }
        if (error.code === status.NOT_FOUND) {
          return { status: 404, body: { code: 'notFound', message: 'Resource not found.' } };
        }
        return {
          status: 503,
          body: { code: 'serviceUnavailable', message: 'A required service is unavailable.' },
        };
      }
      if (typeof error === 'object' && error !== null && 'type' in error) {
        if (error.type === 'entity.too.large')
          return {
            status: 413,
            body: { code: 'requestTooLarge', message: 'AI requests must be at most 500 KB.' },
          };
        if (error.type === 'entity.parse.failed')
          return { status: 400, body: { code: 'invalidAiRequest', message: 'Invalid JSON request.' } };
      }
      return { status: 500, body: { code: 'aiError', message: 'The AI request failed.' } };
    }
    
    @Catch()
    export class AiExceptionFilter implements ExceptionFilter {
      private readonly logger = new Logger(AiExceptionFilter.name);
    
      catch(error: unknown, host: ArgumentsHost) {
        const response = host.switchToHttp().getResponse<Response>();
        const mapped = publicError(error);
        if (mapped.status >= 500) this.logger.error({ err: error }, 'AI request failed');
        if (!response.headersSent) {
          if (mapped.status === 429) response.setHeader('Retry-After', '60');
          response.status(mapped.status).json(mapped.body);
        } else {
          response.end();
        }
      }
    }

    async function bootstrap() {
      const app = await NestFactory.create<NestExpressApplication>(AppModule, {
        bufferLogs: true,
        bodyParser: false,
      });
      const logger = app.get(Logger);
      const configService = app.get(ConfigService);
      app.useLogger(logger);
      app.useBodyParser('json', { limit: 512000 });
      app.useGlobalFilters(new AiExceptionFilter());
      const appConfig = configService.get<AppConfig>(APP_CONFIG);
      if (!appConfig) {
        throw new Error('APP_CONFIG not found');
      }
      const port = appConfig.port;
      app.enableShutdownHooks();
      await app.listen(port);
    
      if (module.hot) {
        module.hot.accept();
        module.hot.dispose(() => app.close());
      }
    }
    
    bootstrap().catch((err) => {
      console.error('Failed to start application', err);
      process.exit(1);
    });
